## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE UNCERTAINTY OF DEVELOPMENTS IN THE SPONSORSHIP AND COMMERCIAL AGREEMENTS MARKET

The Group generates a significant portion of its operating revenues from sponsorship and partnership contracts with a small number of main sponsors (i.e. technical and jersey sponsors) and is therefore greatly exposed to the risk of dependence on the main commercial sponsorship contracts.

Upon expiry or in the event of resolution of these agreements, the Group may not be able to renew or replace them with contracts with similar or better conditions or

![img-41.jpeg](img-41.jpeg)

may not be able to renew or replace them at all. In addition, the sporting results of the First Team, the popularity of Juventus and the reputation of its brands have a significant impact on the possibility of renewing or replacing sponsorship and advertising contracts and on the ability to negotiate similar or better conditions. The Group is also actively competing with other top European clubs in the sponsorship market.

There is a risk that the occurrence of the events described above may have negative impacts, including significant, on the volume of revenues generated by the Group as well as, general speaking, on the economic and financial position of the Group.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH FAILURE TO ACHIEVE INVESTMENT/DISINVESTMENT OBJECTIVES (PLAYER TRADING TRANSACTIONS)

The Group's revenues and cash flows are also significantly influenced by the player trading transactions carried out during the players' transfer campaigns.

The Group is therefore exposed to the risk associated with the management and performance of player trading, which is intrinsically characterised by elements of high uncertainty and variability. Furthermore, players' registration rights represent the Group's most important asset, which is therefore exposed to the risk associated with the management of these rights and, in particular, their expiry and reduction in their market value.

Market conditions and the uncertainty of negotiations could prevent the achievement of the technical-sporting objectives and, at the same time, the net investment targets defined by the Group's economic and financial planning. Equally, it cannot be ruled out a sudden drop in the value of these rights, with the subsequent accounting of write-downs or capital losses in the event of disposals. Furthermore, the failure to optimise the players 'squad' - also conditioned by a possible non-acceptance of transfers to other clubs by Juventus players - could result in higher costs, amortisations and wages higher than forecast or excessive compared to planning estimates. This risk, however, affects all football clubs operating in an environment marked by growing polarisation, with few top clubs

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH A REDUCED APPEAL OF THE JUVENTUS BRAND, WITH A CONSEQUENT LOSS OF COMMERCIAL VALUE AND AN IMPACT ON ALL REVENUE LINES

The Group is exposed to the risk of losing its brand appeal, whose value is deeply rooted in its history, but which is also connected to the maintenance of excellence in some key indicators. In turn, the appeal of Juventus depends on the value and success of the brand. Relations with potential and current sponsors are actually heavily influenced by the popularity of Juventus as a football team and, therefore, also as a brand.

Any reduction in the appeal of the Juventus brand among its fan base and the stakeholders, could have negative impacts on revenues and, if it were to continue, could lead to a poorer-than-expected performance, with consequent negative effects, including significant, on the economic and financial situation of the Group.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE ATTRACTION, RETENTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF TALENTS AND HUMAN CAPITAL

The Group could encounter increasing difficulty in attracting, retaining and incentivising talented people (in both the Football and Corporate areas), or in promptly identifying new key figures to be incorporated in its organisational chart, also in consideration of the instability of the current labour market, with possible negative effects on its reputation, operations and business performance.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ESG PROJECTS AND INITIATIVES

After focusing its efforts on charity and social responsibility initiatives for many years, Juventus has embarked on a broader and more structured sustainability programme based on the progressive integration of Environmental, Social and Governance ("ESG") principles into its business model. This process reflects the growing importance of the issue in corporate strategy, driven in part by changes in the regulatory environment and increasing attention from stakeholders. For further information on this, please refer to the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

During this phase of transition towards a full and systemic integration of sustainability, the Group is committed to ensuring increasingly sound alignment and promoting a shared vision at all organisational levels. However, the risk of incidents of misalignment with ESG values cannot be ruled out, due to operational choices or individual behaviour that is not consistent with the stated objectives. These discrepancies may concern both individuals within the organisation, such as employees and collaborators, and external stakeholders, such as the public attending the stadium. One particularly sensitive area is that of inclusion and non-discrimination where, despite the many initiatives adopted, individual discriminatory behaviour by

## OPERATING/PROCESS RISKS

### RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PLAYERS' SPORTING ACTIVITY, PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH AND PHYSICAL FITNESS

The Group is exposed to the risk associated with players' sporting activity, mental and physical health and physical fitness, as well as the risk that players could suffer serious injuries or bans, also from participating in domestic and international competitions. With reference to physical fitness, special attention must be paid to their training activities and athletic conditioning, in order to reduce the risk of activities not precisely calibrated to the players, generating the possibility of more serious injuries than physiologically conceivable.

The Group is also exposed to risks related to its players' safety during Men's First Team away matches, since any accidents, whether related to travel or the place in which the First Team is staying and playing the matches, could cause significant negative impacts on the squad and its sporting results, with subsequent impacts, including significant, on the economic and financial position of the Group.

### RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE IMPROPER USE OF THE BRAND BY THIRD PARTIES AND THE MANAGEMENT OF INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

The Group is exposed, at global level, to the risk associated with the violation by third parties of its intellectual property rights, including the main registered trademark and all secondary trademarks.

Although the Group pursues a strategy aimed at protecting the Juventus brand and, in general, its intellectual property, against violations by third parties (such as, for example, counterfeiting, piracy or unauthorised use), it cannot be excluded that third parties may improperly use or exploit the trademarks, copyrights, web domains and the brand of the Group, or interfere in other ways with the property rights held, with consequent negative effects on the business, the prospects and the economic and financial situation of the Group.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE COMPROMISE OF IT SECURITY

The Group is subject to the risk of cyber-attacks targeted at (i) compromising IT security with impacts in terms of business interruptions, restoration costs and reputational damages or (ii) taking possession, given the amount of sensitive information processed (including that of an economic, financial, sports and medical nature) of sensitive and/or relevant information, which, if disclosed, could have harmful consequences.

This risk may arise as a consequence of compromising the external perimeter (i.e. all systems accessible from the public internet), undermining the internal perimeter (i.e. all systems within the infrastructure) and compromising the supply chain.

The Group is aware of this risk and monitors the level of security of its information systems and of its own infrastructure, monitoring the security posture of its suppliers and intervening where necessary. Cyber security plans have also been defined for the company's IT assets, along with actions necessary to mitigate the main security risks and training for employees and collaborators in the field of IT security. Dedicated policies and procedures have been produced in accordance with current regulations (including NIS2).

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE MANAGEMENT OF THE ALLIANZ STADIUM AND THE CONDUCT OF THE MATCH EVENT

The Group is exposed to the risk that public access to the Allianz Stadium (which generates revenues from the sale of tickets to attend national and European sporting competitions) may be prohibited or that the stadium may become unusable, even only temporarily, for example, due to infrastructural, technological, health, safety or public order reasons or, in any case, for reasons beyond its control, or is considered an unsafe place by the public. This risk could be all the more amplified the greater the number of services outsourced to third parties, not under the direct control of Juventus.

The Allianz Stadium's structure and the surrounding areas used for parking, as already happened in the past, are also exposed to the risk of damage and/or vandalism, as well as natural phenomena and disasters, and more generally of all those events outside the control of the Group, exposing it to the risk of incurring higher costs or unexpected expenses.

In addition, the Group is exposed to all risks associated with the management of match day events, among which the most relevant is the risk of incurring liability, also from an objective point of view, or penalties due to the behaviour of its fans, with consequent negative effects, including significant, on the Group's business, prospects and economic and financial position. The Group cannot rule out the possibility, in future, that events beyond its control may result in sanctions (including disqualification of a section or the whole stadium, fines, and bans from competitions), with a possible reduction in ticket sales and incurring in extraordinary expenses, nor can it, at the current state of play, evaluate the sports, economic and financial-related consequences that may arise. Furthermore, following these events, the need to consolidate security measures during home matches could arise, with additional costs and expenses for the safety of fans and insurance, and with consequent negative effects on the economic and financial position of the Group, as well as its operations, strategies and prospects.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROTECTION OF THE PHYSICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH OF MINORS

The Group is exposed to the risk associated with the protection of the mental and physical health of minors carrying out sports activities and/or for promotional purposes offered by Juventus or by third-party companies contracted by it.

Specifically, in situations where Juventus is (directly and/or indirectly) responsible for minors, the risk arises from events (such as accidents), also outside of sport activities, which might compromise the physical safety of minors and/or from the possibility that minors may suffer physical or psychological mistreatment or abuse by adults or other minors, with reputational consequences and/or sanctions pursuant to the FIGC/UEFA Guidelines.

## FINANCIAL RISKS
RISKS CONNECTED TO THE GROUP'S FINANCIAL DEBT

### CREDIT RISK

Credit risk essentially derives from trade receivables from customers and receivables from football clubs arising from disposals of players. The Group has appropriate procedures in place to minimise exposure to this risk. In particular, receivables due from Italian football clubs are secured through the clearing house system organised by LCA. Fees receivable under contracts for audiovisual rights instead are, instead, indirectly secured by guarantees given to LCA by the entities that win said rights.

In addition, the Group is also exposed to the risks associated with the non-collection of unsecured receivables, mainly due from sponsors, from which the bulk of its revenues derives, however, concentrated on a relatively small number of counterparties. Should the credit quality of counterparties deteriorate in the future or default rates increase significantly, this could lead to an increase in credit losses and provision for doubtful accounts, with consequent possible negative

effects on the economic and financial situation of the Group. In any case, unsecured trade receivables are constantly monitored. The Group sets aside a provision for doubtful accounts to manage the risk of uncollectability.

### INTEREST RATE RISK

Variable-rate loans expose the Group to the risk that cash flows may fluctuate as a result of changes in interest rates. These financial market risks could affect the Group's financial position and operating results. For this reason, such risks are identified and monitored in order to detect potential negative effects in advance and take the necessary actions to mitigate them.

The financial liabilities that give rise to this risk include bank overdrafts, payables to factoring companies for advances on commercial contracts, and medium-term loans obtained from certain banking institutions.

If interest rates were to rise in the future, this would thus lead to an increase in financial expenses, with consequent possible negative effects on the economic and financial situation of the Group. To mitigate exposure to interest rate fluctuations, the Group regularly monitors market trends, evaluates refinancing opportunities and performs sensitivity analyses on expected cash flows. Furthermore, the Group diversifies its debt maturities in order to avoid concentrations and reduce exposure to refinancing risk in unfavourable contexts. Finally, the Group maintains adequate cash reserves and committed credit lines in order to ensure financial flexibility and reduce the impact of any unfavourable interest rate trends.

### LIQUIDITY RISK

Liquidity risk is the risk that available cash flow may fall short of the obligations and liabilities falling due. The Group manages liquidity risk by keeping the total amount of credit facilities in place with a number of leading credit institutions at a level sufficient to prevent cash flow shortages from arising and ensure that operating and investment requirements are satisfied.

If unfavourable financial market conditions were to restrict the credit facilities available to the Group and force it to exceed its credit limits, this could result in financial stress with possible negative effects on the Group's economic and financial position.

## COMPLIANCE RISKS

### RISKS CONNECTED TO CONDUCT AND/OR INCONSISTENT DECLARATIONS WITH JUVENTUS' VALUES AND COMMUNICATION AND STRATEGIC GUIDELINES BY JUVENTUS PERSONNEL

The Group is heavily exposed to the risk connected to the impacts that the conduct by personnel may have on the reputation of the Group itself. The risk is primarily related to the conduct engaged during sporting events by the subjects most exposed to the media, who, through their statements, behaviour or publications (also using social media) of content that is inconsistent with Juventus' values, and communication and strategic guidelines; this conduct could have a significant impact on the Group's image, reputation and brand, with economic and financial repercussions on the Group.

This risk can also be identified with reference to conduct, declarations, behaviour or publications not necessarily actually held and/or carried out by Juventus staff, whether registered or not (fake news).

This risk is further amplified by the complexity in governing and monitoring the behaviour of individuals associated to Juventus, especially in relation to conduct engaged in contexts not related to the professional activity carried out on behalf of Juventus, but still associated - directly or indirectly - to the image and reputation of the Group itself.

The same risk exists, albeit in a direct and - therefore - more controllable way, in relation to the use of digital communication platforms by the Company itself, which may not be able to manage or make the most of the social media on which it is active.

## RISKS RELATED TO LITIGATION AND PENDING PROCEEDINGS

The Group is a party to certain legal and administrative proceedings. The Group manages and constantly monitors pending proceedings and, on the basis of the outcome that can be predicted for them, proceeds, when necessary, with the allocation of the relative risk provisions.

It should be noted that, as at the date of this annual report, the Company is, among others, party to the following proceedings:

- A. Criminal proceedings pending before the Rome Judicial Authority;
- B. Administrative proceedings initiated by Consol pursuant to Art. 187-septies of Italian Legislative Decree 58/1998.

For further information, including those referred to above, please refer to Note 55 – Relevant pending disputes of the Consolidated Financial Statements as at 30 June 2025 and Note 54 – Relevant pending disputes of the Statutory Financial Statements as at 30 June 2025.

The Group is also exposed to possible risks related to the initiation of inspections and/or new proceedings brought by judicial authorities, supervisory authorities and/or industry bodies (domestic and/or international).

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH NON-COMPLIANCE WITH THE UEFA FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY PARAMETERS AND THOSE ESTABLISHED BY THE FIGC

The Group operates within a complex regulatory framework and is subject to compliance with the regulations of the Serie A League, FIGC (Italian Football Federation), UEFA and FIFA. These rules and regulations cover various aspects of the activities such as the organisation of competitions, requirements and limits regarding the registration of players, as well as certain aspects of their employment relationship with professional football clubs, the management of the Transfer Campaign and the distribution of income from audio-visual rights. The violation or any future changes in the law, the regulations of the Serie A League, FIGC, UEFA, FIFA or other regulations or sudden changes in the current interpretation of the regulations in force, may adversely affect the Group's activities and results as well as the First Team's performance.

Football clubs are also restricted by economic and financial parameters for taking part in championships at national level (Serie A Championship) and European level (including UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League and UEFA Conference League).

Only football clubs, which not only hold the required sporting title, but prove they satisfy the sporting, legal, infrastructural, organisational and economic and financial criteria, are allowed to participate in UEFA competitions, and thus obtain the 'UEFA Licence', pursuant to the UEFA Club Licensing Manual. It acknowledges the recently issued UEFA CL&FS, based on compliance with three main economic and financial parameters:

- 'Squad Cost Ratio', to ensure a better balance between costs incurred and revenues generated by the clubs;
- 'Football Earnings Rule' for achieving break-even in the medium term; and
- 'Overdue Payables', in order to protect creditors and ensure greater solvency of football clubs.

For the 2024 calendar year, the Group respected the Squad Cost Ratio on a consolidated basis (the parameter limit for 2024 was 80%). Based on current estimates of revenues and costs related to the calculation of this parameter and in the absence of non-recurring events, the Group also expects to be able to comply with this parameter for the calendar year 2025 as well (for 2025, the maximum limit for this parameter drops to 70% - the level required when fully operational, which will also apply to future financial years).

With reference to the Football Earning Rule parameter, on 18 September, as is customary in similar situations for clubs participating in UEFA competitions, the Group received notification from UEFA of the opening of proceedings for the potential breach of the same for the three-year period 2022/2023-2024/2025. The outcome of this procedure - which will also take into account the outlook for the current year and future years for all UEFA economic and financial parameters - is expected in spring 2026 and could result in a possible financial penalty (currently difficult to quantify, but presumably not significant) as well as possible sporting restrictions (such, for example, as restrictions on the registration of new players in UEFA competitions).

Finally, for the sake of completeness, it should be noted that the Overdue Payables parameter has always been complied with by the Group and is expected to be complied with in the future as well.

With regard to the point above, it should be noted that, on 28 July 2023, the First Chamber of the UEFA Club Financial Control Body made the decision by which it definitely closed the proceedings initiated on 1 December

At the date of this annual report, no significant breaches of the CL&FS have been identified by Juventus' auditors and/or UEFA.

In Italy, the Financial Sustainability Regulations currently require additional parameters to be met, including a

liquidity indicator ('Liquidity Index'), a debt indicator and an indicator of extended cost of labour.

The liquidity index (i.e. the ratio between current assets and current liabilities) is the main financial/equity parameter provided for by N.O.I.F. Failure to respect this parameter at the reference dates of 31 March and 30 September, to be verified respectively on 31 May and 30 November of each sport season, could place limitations on the acquisitions of players' registration rights for the summer and/or winter sessions, respectively, of each sport season. Based on the information currently available and thanks to the progressive restructuring measures and improvement in the debt structure, the Group expects to be able to comply with the Liquidity Index as at 30 September 2025 on a consolidated basis - as was already the case in the previous report as at 31 March 2025 - and to be able to operate without restrictions in the upcoming winter transfer window.

It is not possible to exclude non-compliance in the future with the metrics indicated above (or new requirements that may be introduced) or that, in order to ensure compliance with the aforementioned metrics, the Group may be forced to source additional financial resources. If the Group is unable to respect the above metrics and/or requirements, it may run the risk of sanctions, management limitations (e.g., limitations on participation in transfer campaign sessions), or in more severe cases, be excluded from participation in domestic and/or European competitions, with significant adverse impacts on its reputation as well as on the economic and financial position of the Group.

Starting from the 2025/2026 sport season, football clubs will also be required to comply with specific criteria related to environmental and social sustainability in order to participate in both national and European competitions and obtain national and UEFA licences. In particular for the purpose of obtaining the:

- National licence, the Company is required to appoint a Social and Environmental Sustainability Officer, responsible for implementing the relevant policies and measures, and a Disability Access Officer, responsible for accessibility for persons with disabilities, who ensures the inclusiveness and accessibility of the facilities and services offered by the Club;
- UEFA Licence, in addition to appointing the above-mentioned figures, the Company is required to submit appropriate documentation certifying the existence of: (i) equality and inclusion policies, (ii) anti-racism policies, (iii) measures to protect minors and young footballers, (iv) measures to promote participation in football to people with different abilities, and (v) environmental sustainability policies.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH CHANGES IN THE TAX FRAMEWORK AND ITS INTERPRETATION

The Group's business is subject to a series of direct and indirect taxes and commissions. The levels of taxation to which the Group's operations are subject may increase or change in the future. Any increases, the introduction of new taxes to which the operations carried out by the Group will be subject, a worsening in preferential tax regimes or uncertainties or changes in the application criteria of current regulations, could have negative effects, including significant, on the business, prospects and the economic and financial position of the Group.

## RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH COMPLIANCE IN RELATION TO DATA PROTECTION

The Group is exposed to the risk of committing violations of the regulations relating to the management, processing and protection of personal data which could lead to sanctions, with possible negative effects on the reputation, as well as on the business, prospects and economic and financial position of the Group.

In carrying out its business, the Group collects, processes and has access on an ongoing basis to personal data - also belonging to special categories - of its fans, customers, employees and entities with whom, for various reasons, it has relationships (i.e. suppliers, consultants, visitors, candidates etc.) as well as players (for example, their health information). The Group must, therefore, comply with the provisions on the processing and free circulation of data indicated by both the European and Italian regulations on the processing of personal data (EU) Regulation no. 679/2016, "GDPR", and Italia Legislative Decree 196/2003, as amended by Italian Legislative Decree 101/2018, "Privacy Code", as well as the provisions of the Italian Data Protection Authority.

The GDPR, in particular, also provides for the significant tightening of administrative monetary sanctions, which for some types of particularly serious violations can be imposed up to the value of € 20 million or 4% of the previous year's total annual turnover, whichever is higher.

# PERSONNEL AND ORGANISATION

## WORKFORCE STRUCTURE

Juventus is aware that a safe, inclusive, open and stimulating working environment that values diversity and is based on developing talent is essential to create a better company. This approach is now formalised in the "People First" pillar of the "Black, White & More" ESG strategy and in the integration (July 2023) of the ESG Team into the People, Culture & ESG Department, to make sustainability an integral part of the daily work of everyone at the Club.

## AS AT 30 JUNE 2025, THERE WERE 538 EMPLOYEES, OF WHOM 399 WERE MEN AND 139 WERE WOMEN.

There are 1,414 non-employees (including 859 trained and available stewards).

For further information on the workforce, please refer to the "Social Information" section of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

## RECRUITING AND ONBOARDING

Juventus has implemented a recruitment and onboarding procedure to ensure structured and transparent processes for selecting and hiring personnel. The policy defines guiding principles and operating rules aimed at promoting meritocracy, fairness and inclusion, ensuring equal opportunities and compliance with current regulations. The process is marked by transparency of information, with clear communication on requirements, responsibilities and growth prospects, and by tools such as Internal Job Posting, which promotes internal mobility and professional development. The Group values strategic networking, as demonstrated by its partnership with MagazziniOz for the employment of persons with disabilities. The selection process is based on objective criteria, practical tests and structured interview cycles, ensuring consistency and impartiality. In a constantly evolving environment, Juventus adopts a flexible and dynamic approach, periodically updating its recruiting strategies to align with emerging best practices and remain competitive in the labour market.

As part of its internal engagement initiatives, the Group has implemented a structured onboarding programme for all new recruits. This plan, divided into modules covering induction, training and organisational orientation, aims to ensure effective and informed integration into the company environment. Onboarding includes activities aimed at understanding the company structure, internal policies and performance expectations, with the aim of promoting productivity and a sense of belonging.

For further information on the recruiting and onboarding process, please refer to the "Social Information" section of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

## COMPANY WELFARE

Juventus promotes organisational wellbeing through policies focused on job protection, remote work as a lever for sustainability and work-life balance, customisable Flexible Benefits plans and wellness initiatives such as the Sport Programme and Fitness Room, to promote employee health and engagement.

For further information on company welfare, please refer to the "Social Information" section of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

## REMUNERATION POLICY (TOTAL REWARD FRAMEWORK)

The preparation, approval and implementation of the remuneration policy ("Remuneration Policy") involve the following bodies and persons, each within their own sphere of competence:

- the Board of Directors;
- the Remuneration and Appointments Committee ("Remuneration and Appointments Committee");
- the Shareholders' Meeting;
- the Board of Statutory Auditors
- the Independent Auditors.

In particular, the Remuneration Policy may first be submitted to the Board of Directors for approval by the Remuneration and Appointments Committee. In drawing up the Policy, the Remuneration and Appointments Committee involves the People, Culture & ESG Department, also with the aim of gathering market data in terms of practices, policies and benchmarking, ensuring

regulatory compliance and improving the preparation of the same policy.

The Group has adopted a remuneration system called the "Total Reward Framework", geared towards the needs and motivations of its human resources, which is based on a so-called banding system, aimed at segmenting company roles in terms of responsibility, level of complexity managed and level of impact on corporate results. The banding system is the cornerstone on which resource management, reward and development processes are built.

The Total Reward Framework consists of: (i) fixed remuneration, (ii) a short-term incentive component (the "STI Plan"), (iii) a long-term incentive component from an equity-based plan (the "LTI Plan"), and (iv) certain benefits and ancillary services.

Both short- and long-term incentive systems have included ESG Key Performance Indicators ("KPIs") within their scorecards.

The Total Reward Framework allows Juventus to guarantee equal work opportunities and fair salary compensation and contract terms to all its resources.

For further information on the remuneration system and policy, please refer to the "Social Information" section of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

## HEALTH AND SAFETY

Juventus adopts a Health and Safety Management System ("HSMS") compliant with the international standard ISO 45001:2018, obtaining its first certification on 25 September 2009 (under the then available OHSAS 18001:2007) as proof of compliance with Italian Legislative Decree 81/08. With a view to continuous improvement, the system is verified annually by the Certification Body through third-party audits.

## QUALITY POLICY FOR THE MEDICAL SECTOR

Not only to achieve its football objectives, but also for the well-being of its employees, Juventus ensures that its athletes and technical staff are in the best possible mental, physical and working conditions. Due to the particular nature of its business, the players' working conditions are a key aspect for the Club. In this sense, Juventus is committed to offering, through innovative structures such as J Medical and Training Centers at Continassa and Vinovo, the best medical-sporting, nutritional and psychological facilities in order to guarantee the highest possible performance levels. Juventus also certifies the achievement of these quality standards through the implementation of its Quality Policy for the Medical Sector, which defines the guidelines and objectives for protecting the Players and the technical sector, under the supervision of the health officer. The Club's Medical Sector has a certified ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System ("QMG"). Its purpose is to protect the health of the athletes in the medical management by the Juventus medical sector in both preventive and therapeutic terms.

## MANAGEMENT AND ORGANISATION OF SPORTING EVENTS

Event management is central to Juventus' business. The Club's facilities can accommodate thousands of people at the same time and with one of the largest fan bases in Italy and Europe, Juventus strongly committed to ensuring the safety and security of its facilities, especially the Stadium and adjacent commercial areas. This activity involves managing complex risks and aims to protect users and operators, strengthening trust and contributing to the achievement of sustainable business objectives over time.

For further information on health and safety, please refer to the "Social Information" section of the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

## EXOR'S EQUITY SUPPORT IN VIEW OF FUTURE CAPITAL INCREASE

It should be noted that the Board of Directors meeting held on 28 March 2025 re-examined the main forecast data as at 31 March and 30 June 2025, as well as possible scenarios relating to the 2025/2026 financial year, taking into account the sports performance of the First Team during the final phase of the third quarter of the 2024/2025 financial year, the impacts arising from the dismissal of the Head Coach and his technical staff, as well as updated sensitivity analysis based on these events. This review highlighted – whilst also taking into account the aforementioned events – a quarterly trend for the 2024/2025 financial year that was different from previous forecasts, as well as greater variability in the economic and financial forecast for the 2024/2025 financial year and the current one.

## THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS HAS THEREFORE PRUDENTLY ASSESSED THE ADVISABILITY OF REQUESTING A STRENGTHENING OF THE COMPANY'S CAPITAL AND FINANCIAL PROFILE

up to a maximum amount equal to 10% of market capitalisation, postponing any resolution until the end of the 2024/2025 sport season and the summer Transfer Campaign.

On the same date, the majority shareholder Exor, confirming its long-term commitment to the Company and its confidence in its intrinsic value, expressed its support for any capital strengthening operation up to its full coverage (and in any case to an extent that at least does not dilute its stake) and made itself available to make equity contributions as an advance of funds of its exclusive competence intended for the release of a Company capital increase. The Board of Directors, having noted Exor's availability, resolved to proceed with the request for a payment on account of a future

capital increase for a total of € 15 million, which was paid by Exor on 31 March 2025.

On 30 June 2025, Exor, at the Company's request, made a second payment on account of a future capital increase for € 15 million, under the same terms, conditions and purposes as the payment made on 31 March (for further information, please refer to the press releases issued by the Company on 28 March and 30 June last, respectively). As agreed, the payments made by Exor are solely for its own account as an advance on sums intended for the release of a capital increase of the Company.

On 26 September 2025, the Board of Directors, also taking into account the actual data for the 2024/2025 financial year and the first phase of the 2025/2026 Transfer Campaign, examined the update of the economic and financial performance estimates for the 2025/2026 financial year and for the subsequent and final year of the 2024/2025 – 2026/2027 Strategic Plan. This update highlighted certain negative variations compared to the original estimates of the plan, which, assuming that the sports performances are consistent with those envisaged in the Strategic Plan and in the absence of non-recurring events, generate the following estimates:

- result and cash-flow for the current year showing a limited improvement compared to the 2024/2025 financial year and, therefore, moderately worse than those forecast in the original plan;
- result and cash-flow for the 2026/2027 financial year in the range of break-even, and therefore slightly worse than those forecast in the original plan.

As a result of the deterioration - compared to the Strategic Plan forecasts - confirmed in 2024/2025 (due to sports performance and sponsorship income lower than the plan's assumptions, as well as non-recurring costs) and expected for 2025/2026 and 2026/2027, and also taking into account the effects of the recently concluded Transfer Campaign, the Board of Directors, following up on what was communicated on 28 March 2025, has resolved to submit to the Shareholders' Meeting to approve the granting - pursuant to Art. 7 of the Company's Articles of Association - of a delegation, ex Art. 2443 of the Italian Civil Code, to the Board of Directors itself to increase the share capital for consideration and divisibly, in one or more tranches, pursuant to Art. 2441, paragraph 4, second sentence, of the Italian Civil Code, within the limits of 10% of the existing share capital. This increase is expected to take place through the issuance of ordinary shares without par value

The Board of Directors will therefore have the possibility to determine, even close to the start of each transaction (i) the amount of the capital increase, in any case not exceeding a maximum amount of 10% of the pre-existing share capital, (ii) the issue price of the shares (including any share premium), which will be determined in compliance with the limits set forth in Art. 2441, paragraph 4, second period, of the Italian Civil Code and (iii) the technical procedures for implementing the capital increase and any placement. The proposed capital increase is part of the actions foreseen by the Strategic Plan and is primarily aimed at (i) strengthening the capital structure, (ii) supporting the achievement of the objectives set out in the Strategic Plan and (iii) maintaining sporting competitiveness.

## FRONT JERSEY SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENTS UNTIL 30 JUNE 2028

On 13 May 2025, Juventus, Stellantis Europe and Visit Detroit reached agreements for front jersey sponsorship until 30 June 2028.

The agreement with Stellantis Europe provides for the use of the Jeep brand as main sponsor of the match jersey for the Men's First Team, Women's First Team and NextGen, for all national, UEFA, and FIFA sporting competitions, starting from the final phase of the 2024/2025 sport season (including the FIFA Club World Cup) and for the 2025/2026, 2026/2027 and 2027/2028 sport seasons.

The agreement provides for a total fixed consideration of € 69 million (of which € 4 million for the final phase of the 2024/2025 sport season, € 19 million for the 2025/2026 sport season, and € 23 million for each of the two subsequent sport seasons), in addition to moderate variable components (penalty) in case of non-participation in UEFA sports competitions.

The Company has also concluded the agreement with Visit Detroit to occupy the second space reserved for sponsors on the front of the match jersey for the Men's First Team, Women's First Team and NextGen, for all national sporting competitions (excluding, therefore, UEFA and FIFA competitions), with the same duration as the Jeep agreement. The agreement with Visit Detroit provides for a total fixed consideration significantly lower than the Jeep sponsorship agreement (in line with the lesser sponsorship rights granted) and variable components (bonus), potentially significant, based on the achievement of certain objectives.

## MANAGEMENT AND COORDINATION ACTIVITIES

Juventus is not subject to management and coordination activities pursuant to Art. 2407 of the Italian Civil Code by its majority shareholder, Exor, as the latter does not take part in the management of the Company's business and acts solely as a shareholder, holding and managing its investment. There is no evidence of any de facto exercise of management and coordination activities, since, among other factors, the Company has full and independent negotiating au-

tonomy in its dealings with third parties, and no centralised treasury relationship exists. Furthermore, the number and professional expertise of the independent directors are appropriate in relation to the size of the Board of Directors and the nature of the Company's activities, thereby ensuring the Board's managerial independence in determining Juventus' general and operational strategic guidelines.

Integrating the Consolidated Sustainability Statement and the annual financial statements have a strategic meaning for the Club, as well as a meaning of compliance being a legal obligation, which consists in being able to explain in a consistent, rigorous and at the same time engaging way why sustainability is important for Juventus. # METRICS SUBJECT TO HIGH LEVEL OF UNCERTAINTY

It should be noted that in some cases the figures could show rounding due to the representation in thou-

sands/million. In addition, it is specified that the quantitative metrics of Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions and the amount of water collected and stored, referring to metrics E1-6 and E3-5, are based on estimates and proxies subject to a high level of uncertainty. With reference to the quantification of Scope 3 emissions, input data were used for the calculation: primary data (category 1 "Purchased goods and services", category 3 "Extraction of fuel and energy", category 4 "Upstream transportation and distribution", category 6 "Business travel" and category 15 "Investments") and proxies calculated starting from a sample of primary data (category 5 "Production scraps and waste", category 7 "Personnel commuting", category 11 "Utilisation and use of the service/product"). There are no quantitative input data based on indirect sources. With reference to data on the quantity of water stored (ref. E3-5), these were estimated on the basis of the capacity of the collection tank (and the artificial pond) and the water consumption from them.

To improve the accuracy of these metrics, the Club plans to implement actions aimed at collecting primary data directly from suppliers, updating calculation methodologies with more advanced models and developing monitoring and traceability systems to reduce dependence on indirect estimates.

# GOVERNANCE AND STRATEGY MODEL

Juventus is aware of the importance of a good Corporate Governance ("Corporate Governance") system for achieving strategic targets and creating long-term sustainable value, ensuring effective governance respecting the institutions and rules, efficient governance in consideration of the principles of economy, and correct governance for all stakeholders in the life of the Company and the Juventus Group (the "Group" or "Juventus Group"). Consistently, the Club maintains its Corporate Governance system constantly in line with relevant recommendations and regulations, adhering to national and international best practices. In addition, Juventus has implemented principles, rules and procedures that govern and guide the performance of the activities of all organisational and operational structures, as well as ensuring that each operation is carried out effectively and transparently.

# GOV-1 – THE ROLE OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE, MANAGEMENT AND SUPERVISORY BODIES

Juventus' corporate governance system, comprising rules and methodologies for planning, management and control, which are necessary for the Company's functioning, was defined by the Board of Directors ("Board of Directors") in compliance with regulations applicable to the Company as a listed issuer, as well as in compliance with the Corporate Governance Code and the national and international best practices applicable to the Company.

The Club adopts a traditional management and control system that provides for a division of competences across the Shareholders' Meeting, the Board of Directors and the Board of Statutory Auditors ("Board of Statutory Auditors"). Moreover, the Board of Directors has set up three internal committees to advise and make proposals to them: the Control and Risk Committee ("Control and Risk Committee") (which also performs the functions of the committee for transactions with related parties, in accordance with the Consob Regulation on related-party transactions, the "Consob RPT Regulation"), the Remuneration and Appointments Committee ("Remuneration and Appoint-

ments Committee") and the Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance Committee ("ESG Committee").

For information regarding how these roles and responsibilities with regard to IROs are reported within the corporate strategy and related policies, please refer to the section "Juventus' approach to sustainability: Black, White & More".

Policies are mainly reported in the section "Governance Information" and in the various sections of the document dedicated to specific ESG policies.

In addition,

# FROM THIS REPORTING PERIOD, THE ROLE OF EXECUTIVE MANAGER ("EXECUTIVE MANAGER")

who, together with the Risk & Compliance and Internal Audit team, oversees the processes related to the IROs, including procedures and controls, was established.

# FOLLOWING CONSULTATION WITH THE ESG COMMITTEE, THE ESG TARGETS ARE APPROVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AS ARE THE METRICS RELATING TO THE PROGRESS

in achieving these targets when approving the Consolidated Sustainability Statement.

# BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Pursuant to Art. 17 of the Articles of Association ("Articles of Association"), the Board of Directors is vested with the broadest powers for ordinary and extraordinary management. It thus has the power to take all the measures considered necessary and appropriate to achieve the Company purposes with no exceptions, save for only the actions reserved to the Shareholders' Meeting according to the law.

In addition to issuing non-convertible bonds, the Board of Directors is also responsible for taking resolutions concerning all transactions permitted by Art. 2365, paragraph 2 of the Italian Civil Code, and their splitting according to the provisions of the law.

In particular, pursuant to the Articles of Association, management is entrusted to a Board of Directors composed of a number of members that may vary from three to 15, according to the determination of the Shareholders' Meeting. The Board of Directors in office at the end of the financial year (i.e. 30 June 2025) was appointed by the Shareholders' Meeting on 18 January 2023. In this

context, only the list of the majority shareholder EXOR N.V. ("Exor"), holder of 63.8% of the ordinary shares at the reporting date, was submitted.

The Board of Directors consists of an Executive Director and four Non-Executive Directors. All non-executive Directors other than the Chair ("Chair") are independent (60%) both pursuant to Art. 148, paragraph 3, of Italian Legislative Decree No. 58 of 24 February 1998 (the Italian Consolidated Law on Finance), and pursuant to Art. 2, recommendation No. 7 of the Corporate Governance Code. The number and competences of the non-executive directors are such as to ensure that they have significant weight in taking board resolutions and to guarantee effective monitoring of management as at 30 June 2025. Three members of the Board of Directors are men and 2 women (representing 40% of the members of the Board of Directors), in compliance with the provisions of the gender regulations on the composition of corporate bodies applicable at the time of the appointment of the Board of Directors in office. In addition, two Directors are under 55 years of age, one belongs to the 55-65 age group and two to the over 65 age group.

# BOARD OF STATUTORY AUDITORS

Pursuant to the Articles of Association, the Board of Statutory Auditors is made up of three Statutory Auditors and two Alternate Auditors; it monitors compliance with the law and the Articles of Association as well as with principles of correct management. It also verifies the adequacy of the Company's organisational structure for aspects relating to the internal control system and administrative and accounting system, in addition to the reliability of the latter in correctly reporting company operations.

The Board of Statutory Auditors carries out also the functions assigned by applicable regulations to the Internal Control and Auditing Committee, established by Italian Legislative Decree no. 39 of 27 January 2010. In this role the Board of Statutory Auditors supervises: (i) the financial disclosure process, (ii) the effectiveness of the internal control, internal audit and risk manage-

ment systems, (iii) the statutory audit of the annual accounts, (iv) the independence of the independent auditors, verifying compliance with applicable regulations, as well as the nature and extent of services other than auditing provided to the Company and its subsidiaries by the same independent auditors and by entities in its network. The Board of Statutory Auditors is then asked to provide a justified proposal to the Shareholders' Meeting at the time of granting and revocation of the statutory audit mandate.

In accordance with the provisions of the law and Art. 22 of the Articles of Association, the Board of Statutory Auditors is appointed on the basis of the lists of candidates lodged at the Company offices by the twenty-fifth day before the date of the Shareholders' Meeting, in which the candidates are listed by a progressive number. The list is divided into two sections: one is for standing statutory auditor candidates and the other is for alternate statutory auditor candidates, in a number no higher than the number of auditors to be elected.

On 7 November 2024, the Shareholders' Meeting appointed the Board of Statutory Auditors for the three-year period 2024/2025 – 2026/2027. On the basis of the only list submitted by the shareholder Exor (holder of 65.4% of ordinary shares at the submission date), the following were appointed as auditors: Roberto Spada, as Standing Auditor and Chair of the Board of Statutory Auditors; Maria Luisa Mosconi and Roberto Petrignani, as Standing Auditors; Stefania Bettoni and Guido Giovanile, as Alternate Auditors. The list, together with the documents required by the Articles of Association for its filing, is available on the website www.juventus.com and on the authorised storage site "1info" www.1info.it.

# INTERNAL COMMITTEES OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Three Committees have been created within the Board of Directors to provide advisory services and proposals:

- the Remuneration and Appointments Committee and the Control and Risk Committee, established in accordance with the Corporate Governance Code. To examine matters relating to the appointment of Directors and issues regarding remuneration, also for the top management, the Board of Directors decided to establish a single Committee as these issues are closely related;
- the ESG Committee, set up on a voluntary basis;
- the Control and Risk Committee is also responsible for transactions with related parties (as defined pursuant to the Consob Related-Party Regulations and for which in fact it also performs the function of committee for transactions with related parties, in accordance with the Consob RPT Regulation) with the exception of those relating to remuneration, which is the responsibility of the Company's Remuneration and Appointments Committee.

The operating procedures, tasks and powers of the Committees are governed by specific regulations approved by the Board of Directors. In performing their functions, the Committees may access any information, which they require, also assisted by

relative company departments. No functions attributed by the Corporate Governance Code to one or more committees are reserved to the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors has defined the composition of each Committee by prioritising the expertise and experience of its members.

# SUSTAINABILITY GOVERNANCE

WITH THE AIM OF CONSTANTLY IMPROVING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF ITS COMPANY ACTIVITIES AND RELATED COMMUNICATIONS TO STAKEHOLDERS, JUVENTUS HAS SET UP AN ESG COMMITTEE, APPOINTED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND ACTIVE SINCE 2022.

The ESG Committee is composed of three members of the Board of Directors, all with the professional expertise and skills appropriate to the tasks assigned to them and is supported in the performance of its functions by the People, Culture & ESG department as well as, if necessary, by external consultants. At the meeting on 24 February 2022, the Board of Directors approved the regulation that governs the operation of the ESG Committee.

The ESG Committee makes proposals and provides advice to the Board of Directors regarding sustainability, in order to promote the gradual integration of environmental, social and governance factors (understood with reference to sustainability) into company activities geared towards the pursuit of sustainable success, and therefore the creation of long-term value for the benefit of shareholders, taking account of the interests of the other stakeholders. In this sense, it is understood to be the body responsible for monitoring the IROs identified by Juventus.

The ESG Committee meets as often as necessary to carry out its activities (in general, at least twice a year, at the times the Consolidated Sustainability Statement drafting process begins and ends), usually on the dates set out in the annual calendar of meetings prepared by the same Committee and, in any case, whenever the Chair of the ESG Committee deems it appropriate or it is requested by the Chair of the Board of Directors, by the Chief Executive Officer or by at least two members of the Committee, for the discussion of a specific topic that they consider to be within the scope of the same Committee.

The ESG Committee has several key responsibilities:

- supports the Board of Directors in defining the sustainability strategy, by preventively and periodically examining the Company's business plan and formulating proposals for the integration of environmental, social and governance factors into the Company's overall business strategy, including therein issues relating to climate change. Juventus' ESG strategy, called Black, White & More, was defined during the 2023/2024 season; for more details, please refer to the specific section of this Consolidated Sustainability Statement;
- verifies the alignment of the company's corporate

governance system with applicable laws and regulations, the recommendations of the Corporate Governance Code and the national and international best practices on sustainability;

- expresses guidelines regarding the initiatives and programmes promoted by the Company to integrate environmental, social and governance factors in the business processes and periodically monitors their performance;
- examines, prior to the meeting of the Board of Directors, the Consolidated Sustainability Statement, containing non-financial information pursuant to (EU) Directives 2014/95 and 2020/852, evaluating the structuring of their associated contents, as well as the completeness and transparency of the communication provided to stakeholders;
- monitors, in coordination with the Control and Risk Committee, the risks and opportunities regarding sustainability linked to environmental, social and governance factors;
- promotes the Company's participation in sustainability and responsible innovation initiatives and events, in order to enhance the Company's reputation regarding sustainability in the national and international domain;
- monitors the Company's positioning on financial markets regarding sustainability, with particular reference to the main ESG ratings and specialised sustainability indexes;
- supports the dissemination of a sustainability culture among employees, shareholders and, more generally speaking, stakeholders;
- expresses, at the request of the Board of Directors or the Chief Executive Officer, opinions on matters which may have an impact on sustainability and responsible innovation issues;
- supports the Control and Risk Committee in assessing the suitability of periodic non-financial information, in correctly representing the business model, the Company strategies, the impact of its activities and

ESG FUNCTION

SINCE STARTING ITS PATH IN SUSTAINABILITY, JUVENTUS HAS CHOSEN TO FACE IT IN A STRUCTURED AND CONCRETE WAY, BY ESTABLISHING A DEDICATED FUNCTION WITH A SPECIALISED TEAM.

Starting from 1 July 2023, this function was incorporated into the People & Culture Department (now "People, Culture & ESG"), marking a symbolic step that reflects the awareness that only through full internal sharing of ESG values can a positive, credible and lasting impact be generated on the outside.

"SUSTAINABILITY IS NOT AN EXCLUSIVE RESPONSIBILITY OF A DEDICATED TEAM, BUT A RESPONSIBILITY SHARED BY EACH PERSON WITHIN THE ORGANISATION"

To effectively monitor ESG issues – also in response to the progressive strengthening of the European and national regulatory framework – Juventus has internally assigned the responsibility of Chief People, Culture & ESG Officer as well as of Head of ESG. These figures are responsible for guiding the strategic integration of sustainability within the various company functions, ensuring consistency between long-term targets, operational activities and key reporting standards. The role includes continuous and transversal coordination, aimed at ensuring a structured, measurable approach and in line with stakeholders' expectations.

In addition, for the purposes of legal certifications to be issued, the Company has formalised the position

The Football Social Responsibility Officer ("FSRO") is responsible for coordinating and promoting social and environmental initiatives, ensuring the integration of social responsibility into the daily activities of the Club and serving as an operational link between the various corporate areas involved.

At the same time, to strengthen dialogue with its community with disabilities and ensure a truly inclusive experience, Juventus has introduced a Disability Access Officer ("DAO"). The DAO is the direct point of contact with fans with disabilities and works to improve accessibility both in the facilities and in the communication channels, with a view to active listening and continuous improvement.

The structure adopted by the Club reflects a cross-functional and long-term oriented model, in which sustainability is transversal leverage involving people, processes and external relations, contributing to the creation of shared value.

# SHAREHOLDERS' MEETING

The Shareholders' Meeting is the body through which shareholders can actively participate in the company's life by expressing their will in the manner and on the matters reserved to them by law and the Articles of Association. The Shareholders' Meeting meets in ordinary and extraordinary session. Resolutions passed in compliance with law and the Articles of Association are binding for all shareholders, including those that are absent or in disagreement, within the limits of the same Articles of Association.

The Shareholders' Meeting resolves on the matters

reserved to it by law and therefore mainly on: (i) in ordinary session, among other things, (a) the financial statements and allocation of the result for the financial year, (b) the appointment and dismissal of Directors, determining their number within the limits set by the Articles of Association and their compensation, (c) the appointment of Statutory Auditors, determining their compensation, and (d) the granting of the statutory audit mandate, on the recommendation of the Board of Statutory Auditors; and (e) in extraordinary session, among other things (a) amendments to the Articles of Association not relating to regulatory adjustments, and (b) transactions of an extraordinary nature, such as, for example, capital increases, mergers and/or demergers.

The Shareholders' Meeting is usually convened by the Board of Directors. In line with the relevant legal provisions, the Articles of Association require the Board to convene the Shareholders' Meeting to approve the financial statements within 120 days of the end of the financial year; in the cases allowed by law, this term can be extended to one 180 days. The ordinary or extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting is also convened whenever the Board of Directors deem it appropriate, and in all cases provided for by law. For further information, please refer to Art. 9 of the Articles of Association, attached to this document, as well as to the 2024/2025 Report on Corporate Governance and Ownership Structure.

# GOV-2 - INFORMATION PROVIDED TO AND SUSTAINABILITY MATTERS ADDRESSED BY THE UNDERTAKING'S ADMINISTRATIVE, MANAGEMENT AND SUPERVISORY BODIES

The administrative, management and supervisory bodies of Juventus are informed at least annually of the IROs material to the activities of the Club.

The ESG Committee submits the relevant documentation to the Board of Directors whenever it is deemed necessary to include an ESG initiative in the sustainability plan ("Sustainability Plan") and/or the 2024/2025 - 2026/2027 strategic plan ("Strategic Plan"), to adopt a new policy and to take a strategic decision in relation to ESG.

The double materiality assessment (see paragraph "Impact, risk and opportunity management") remains the starting point for the prioritisation of actions within the Sustainability Plan carried out by the Company, under the supervision of the relevant Committees and the Board of Directors.

# GOV-3 - INTEGRATION OF SUSTAINABILITY-RELATED PERFORMANCE IN INCENTIVE SCHEMES

The preparation, approval and implementation of the remuneration policy ("Remuneration Policy") involve the following bodies and persons, each within their own sphere of competence:

- the Board of Directors;
- the Remuneration and Appointments Committee;
- the Shareholders' Meeting;
- the Board of Statutory Auditors; and
- the independent auditors.

In particular, the Remuneration Policy may first be submitted to the Board of Directors for approval by the Remuneration and Appointments Committee. In drawing up the Policy, the Remuneration and Appointments Committee involves the People, Culture & ESG Department, also with the aim of gathering market data in terms of practices, policies and benchmarking, ensuring regulatory compliance and improving the preparation of the same policy and, where necessary, also independent experts on the topic. Furthermore, the ESG Committee expresses its opinion on the ESG performance targets of the variable incentive schemes.

# THE COMPANY HAS ADOPTED A REMUNERATION SYSTEM ENTITLED THE TOTAL REWARD FRAMEWORK ("TOTAL REWARD FRAMEWORK"), ORIENTED TO THE NEEDS AND MOTIVATIONS OF RESOURCES,

defining a set of tools that allow to outline reward strategies tailored to and consistent with the different workforce clusters, within a single, fair and transparent structure.

More specifically, the Total Reward Framework is based on a "banding" system. The system divides company roles into eight different bands (i.e. contiguous

classes of jobs) which are assessed according to Mercer's International Positioning Evaluation (IPE) method and include consistent roles in terms of responsibility, level of complexity managed and level of impact on corporate results.

The banding system is the cornerstone on which resource management, reward and development processes are built.

The Total Reward Framework consists of: (i) fixed remuneration, (ii) a short-term incentive component (the "STI Plan") represented by an annual short-term monetary incentive component intended, inter alia, for the Chief Executive Officer and key management personnel, (iii) a long-term incentive component deriving from a plan based on financial instruments intended, in its first allocation cycle, for a select group of key resources, including the Chief Executive Officer and key management personnel and other employees with strategic roles within the Company or its subsidiaries (the "STI Plan"), and (iv) certain benefits and ancillary services.

# BOTH SHORT- AND LONG-TERM INCENTIVE SYSTEMS HAVE INCLUDED ESG KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS ("KPIS") WITHIN THEIR SCORECARDS.

Specifically with regard to the STI Plan structured with a single scorecard, consisting of three macro-targets: an economic-financial KPI, strategic KPIs for each function and an ESG KPI, as an individual target relating to environmental sustainability parameters, promotion of a sustainable culture and reduction of operating costs. In particular, the target identified for the 2024/2025 financial year (in line with the Company's ESG Strategy & Framework) is to reduce energy consumption at the Company's sites, to be assessed by comparing the energy consumption of the year of the baseline (figure as at 30 June 2024) with those at the end of the 2024/2025 financial year (as at 30 June 2025). In the STI Plan, the ESG component has a weight of 10% on total remuneration.

Also in the LTI Plan, which has a multi-year duration (until 31 December 2029) and is divided into the following three vesting periods, according to a rolling attribution logic: (i) 1 July 2024 – 30 June 2027; (ii) 1 July 2025 – 30 June 2028; and (iii) 1 July 2026 – 30 June 2029, it is envisaged in particular that the rights attributed will vest if specific economic-financial, return on shares and ESG targets are achieved. In the LTI Plan the ESG component has a weight of 15% on total remuneration with reference to the first allocation cycle and will have a weight of 10% with reference to the second allocation cycle.

The target based on the ESG KPI has been identified in obtaining and maintaining the Gender Equality Certification (PdR UNI 125:2022), introduced by the National Recovery and Resilience Plan ("NRRP"), the Italian plan of investments and reforms within the European programme Next Generation EU that defines the guidelines on the management system for gender equality.

The measurement of the certification is conducted at the beginning and end of the vesting period on the basis of specific qualitative and quantitative indicators and access to the certification by the Certifying Body is envisaged in the event that a minimum overall summary score of at least 60% is achieved.

The Total Reward Framework allows Juventus to guarantee all its resources the same work opportunities and fair salary compensation and contract terms.

# GOV-4 – STATEMENT ON DUE DILIGENCE

As mentioned in the previous paragraphs, during the 2023/2024 season Juventus developed its ESG strategy "Black, White & More", the result of an in-depth benchmark activity with football clubs, other sports clubs, entertainment companies and important ESG players.

Juventus presented its strategy during the 2024/2025 season, with a dedicated event on 17 December 2024 open to external stakeholders and preceded by an internal roadshow aimed at all company managers.

The strategy was built in dialogue with top management and has - among its various objectives - the objective of strengthening integration of ESG issues into the Club's business model and operations.

The integration model developed is divided into four levels:

# DIRECTION

# ESG BOARD COMMITTEE

It supports the Board of Directors in defining a sustainability strategy, making proposals for integration into the overall strategy of Juventus; examines, together with the Control and Risk Committee, the Consolidated Sustainability Statement, evaluating the contents, completeness and transparency of communication; promotes a culture of sustainability among all stakeholders of the Club.

# LEADERSHIP

# ESG STEERING COMMITTEE

It promotes cross-alignment between all Impact Teams ("Impact Teams") involved in projects and initiatives with ESG impact, promoting an integrated approach to sustainability. It approves the ESG targets of the Impact Teams and monitors their achievement; it promotes the cascading of ESG targets and priorities within the organisation. The Steering Committee, announced at the launch of the People First policy (see S1 policies), also plays a supervisory role on diversity, equity and inclusion issues.

# ACTION

# ESG IMPACT TERMS OWNER

It ensures the integration of ESG targets into the operational activities of the most relevant company teams. In this perspective, Juventus emphasises that "sustainability is not an exclusive responsibility of the ESG team, but a responsibility shared by each person within the organisation". The success of the sustainability strategy thus passes through the daily contribution that each colleague can make. The Impact Teams, identified in the areas of highest impact, started a first round of work with two meetings held in July 2025; by November the assignment of the first specific targets will be completed, in what represents a year of adjustment of the model.

# ENGAGEMENT

# POSITIVE IMPACT HUB

A group of 12 people, selected following a voluntary application, promotes the conception and development of bottom-up initiatives on ESG issues, serving as ambassadors of positive change and promoting the dissemination of sustainability and well-being initiatives in the community. The announcement of the Positive Impact Hub was communicated in the e-mail to disseminate the People First policy, with an application process concluded in June 2025 and official training in July, the month in which the first meeting was held. Subsequent meetings are already planned, starting in September.

## GOV-5 – RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROLS OVER SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING

### RISK MANAGEMENT

The Company has implemented a risk management process through the adoption of an ERM model that allows the identification, assessment and management of business risks on an ongoing basis (hereinafter also referred to as “Risk Assessment”). This model is aligned with the recommendations of the Corporate Governance Code for listed companies and international best practices.

The Risk Assessment activities conducted have identified risks with a potential impact on sustainability issues. Each of these risks is precisely classified with the relevant topical standard (E, S, G) and with the material topics identified by Juventus.

These risks were assessed and managed according to the risk management methodology adopted by the Company, in line with the double materiality assessment carried out, as described in the section SBM-2 – “Disclosure Requirement – Interests and views of stakeholders”.

## INTERNAL CONTROLS ON SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING

The Risk & Compliance and Internal Audit Department, in support of the Executive Manager responsible for preparing sustainability reports and as required by the “Sustainability reporting preparation” procedure, performed internal controls on the Consolidated Sustainability Statement in relation to the following topics: energy consumption and mix (E1-5 – Energy consumption and mix), water consumption (E3-4 – Water consumption) and resource outflows (E5-5 – Resource outflows).

The objective of the internal controls was to provide assurance regarding the completeness and consistency of the data source as well as the accuracy of the collection process carried out by the relevant functions.

Juventus undertakes to progressively implement a structured and formalised system of internal control over Consolidated Sustainability Reporting.

# **SBM-1 - STRATEGY, BUSINESS MODEL AND VALUE CHAIN**

Juventus is a professional football club listed on Borsa Italiana S.p.A. that, during its more than century-long history, has established itself as one of the most winning and recognised teams at a national and international level, consisting of 538 employees and a revenue of € 529,630 thousand. The Company's core business is participation in domestic and international football competitions and the organisation of matches. The main sources of revenues come from the licensing of audiovisual and media rights (in relation to the matches played), sponsorships, revenues from the stadium and friendly matches; trademark licensing for marketing products; as well as the marketing of additional services to fans. Moreover, the Company earns additional income from the management of players' registration rights.

It should also be noted that pursuant to IFRS 8 - Operating Segments, the Group's main business segment is participation in domestic and international football competitions; as a consequence, the economic, equity and financial components of the financial statements can be attributed essentially to this type of activity. Furthermore, Juventus' business activity is primarily carried out in Italy. For further information on the composition of the workforce, please refer to the section "Social Information (S1)".

Juventus' shares are listed on the Euronext Milan, a regulated market organised and managed by Borsa Italiana S.p.A. ("EXM").

Juventus' business model is structured on the following Cash Generating Units (CGUs): sports activities linked to the playing of national and international competitions (Juventus) and hotel activities (J-Hotel). Both these activities are valued from the point of view of the sustainability performance of this document, as well as within the value chain.

Football has more fans in the world than any other sport. Competitive football is organised on a global scale by FIFA, and includes multiple federations. FIFA delegates part of its powers to continental confederations, including UEFA in Europe, which organises not only European competitions between nations, but also those between clubs, including the UEFA Champions League.

At the individual country level, football is headed by a national federation which is a member of UEFA and FIFA. In Italy, this reference federation is the FIGC (Italian Football Federation), which is recognised by CONI (Italian National Olympic Committee).

Within this context, Juventus plays a significant role in the football industry on a national and international level. The Club's commitment is reflected in its active participation in various prestigious associations and competitions, confirming its contribution to the growth and development of football.

**FIFA:** In the 2024/2025 season, Juventus' first men's team participated in the first edition of the FIFA Club World Cup 2025, an event of great prestige that highlights the international importance of the Club, reaching the round of 16 of the competition.

**UEFA:** In the 2025/2026 season, the Men's First Team will take part in the UEFA Champions League. In the new format launched during the 2024/2025 season, 36 teams compete in a single league round; clubs ranked from 1st to 8th at the end of the league phase, which includes eight single matches, qualify for the round of 16; clubs ranked from 9th to 24th qualify for the knock-out phase play-offs; clubs ranked from 25th to 36th are permanently eliminated from Europe for the current season.

The Women's First Team will instead participate in the UEFA Women's Champions League, consolidating the Club's presence in the women's football elite. Also in this case, UEFA has planned a change in format starting from the 2025/2026 season, which aligns with the men's one.

**FIGC:** Juventus contributes to the development and regulation of Italian football by actively collaborating with the FIGC.

**ECA:** Juventus is a member of the ECA, co-operating with the association to improve conditions and opportunities for European clubs.

**Lega Serie A:** Juventus is an active member of Lega Serie A, participating in and adding its expertise to the development and governance of Italy's premier football league. In addition to the Serie A championship, the Men's First Team participates in Coppa Italia, a competition that makes Juventus' presence in the national football scene even more valuable.

**Women's Serie A:** The Women's First Team is involved in the Serie A championship, strengthening its role in promoting movement in Italy. The women's team also participates in the relative Coppa Italia. In the season just ended, the team won the title and the Coppa Italia.

**Lega Pro:** Juventus was the first Club in Italy to invest in a second team thanks to the successful project launched in 2018. Named Juventus Next Gen, the team will participate in group B of Lega Pro in the 2025/2026 season and in Serie C in the Coppa Italia.

# **JUVENTUS' APPROACH TO SUSTAINABILITY: BLACK, WHITE & MORE**

**JUVENTUS' ESG STRATEGY, CALLED BLACK, WHITE & MORE, REFLECTS THE CLUB'S IDENTITY, ITS ROLE IN THE COMPANY AND THE DESIRE TO GENERATE A POSITIVE IMPACT WELL BEYOND THE PITCH.**

Based on six pillars, the strategy allows for the gradual integration of ESG principles in all the activities of the Club, whether or not they are directly related to sport, contributing to the creation of long-term value for Juventus and all of its stakeholders.

**Black, White & More** is both philosophy and an operational framework. It starts with the awareness that, as a benchmark in the global sports scene, Juventus has a duty to take on increasing responsibilities towards the community, the planet and future generations. In this perspective:

Juventus is *Black, White & Green* when it works with other organisations to combat climate change;

It is *Black, White & Orange* when it engages against all forms of violence against women;

It is *Black, White & Rainbow* when it promotes and defends the rights of LGBTQIA+ people;

It is also *Black, White & More* for all the topics that testify to the Club's desire to contribute to a fairer, safer and more sustainable world.
