# PUBLISHED THE "PEOPLE FIRST" POLICY, A POLICY DOCUMENT WITH WHICH THE CLUB REAFFIRMS ITS COMMITMENT TO FOCUSING ON PEOPLE BOTH ON AND OFF THE PITCH

The target is to ensure an inclusive, fair, respectful and safe environment for anyone who works, plays, supports or collaborate with the Company. Under the responsibility of the People, Culture & ESG Chief, the Policy protects the rights and dignity of people, challenging all forms of discrimination and violence, and actively promoting diversity, inclusion, gender equality and accessibility.

With People First, Juventus aims to ensure equal opportunities for all, fostering an environment where each individual can feel welcomed, valued and an integral part of the Juventus community. Football is thus conceived as an open space, without barriers, where to educate players, employees and fans to use respectful language and share common values. The Club intends to set itself as an example of sustainability and social responsibility, translating these principles into concrete actions.

The policy envisages the adoption of clear rules against all forms of discrimination, harassment or racism, together with the introduction of fair and transparency-based selection and management processes for staff. Regular training courses are planned, focusing on equity and inclusion, the implementation of internal controls and the possibility of anonymous reports through dedicated channels. In addition to this, there are projects aimed at improving stadium accessibility, promoting women's football and collaborating with local social organisations.

The policy applies to all people who come into contact with Juventus: employees, players, fans, partners, suppliers and members of the community. The target is to build, day by day, an environment where respect, inclusion and equal opportunities are shared and con-

cretely pursued values.

Demonstrating that the principles of the policy are not something that remain on paper, Juventus translates them into concrete initiatives that produce measurable results.

In this sense, the achievement of the UNI/PdR 125:2022 certification for gender equality, obtained by in June 2025 with a total score of 74/100 following an audit conducted by Bureau Veritas, represents not only an important formal milestone, but also a concrete confirmation of the Club's commitment to a fair, inclusive and sustainable work environment. Recognised at national level as an official reference on gender equality, this certification attests the adoption of a structured system for gender equality governance, based on objective indicators in key areas such as careers opportunities, pay equity, work-life balance, protection of parents and inclusive culture.

Juventus will continue to monitor and improve its performance in this field, with the target of consolidating an organisational culture that fully values each person.

Among the policies adopted by Juventus to ensure structured and consistent management of its own workforce, a key role is played by the Recruitment & Onboarding Procedure, which governs the processes for selecting and hiring staff with a subordination contract. Under the responsibility of the People, Culture & ESG Chief, the procedure defines guiding principles, golden rules and specific operational methods, with the target of ensuring effective, inclusive and transparent management of new employees, promoting a quality experience, engaging and consistent with the Club's culture.

In Juventus, people represent the beating heart of the organisation and the driver of its success. For this reason, recruiting is structured to attract and enhance talent, offering candidates a real, inclusive and engaging experience that allows them to fully express their potential. The entire selection and onboarding process is based on a series of core principles that guide each stage of the process:

- Meritocracy, fairness and inclusion: Juventus is committed daily to promoting an open and respectful working environment, where diversity is deemed a resource and every person is valued for what they are. The selection process is based on objective and meritocratic criteria, ensuring equal opportunities for all applicants, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, civil status or parenting. The skills, experience and background of each candidate are central elements in their assessment. In addition, mandatory hires are managed in full compliance with current regulations and company needs, with the adoption of policies aimed at promoting inclusion, equal treatment and organisational well-being.

- Transparency and clear communication: Juventus pays great attention to clarity and transparency at every stage of the selection process. Detailed information on the requirements, expected responsibilities, remuneration ranges and growth prospects is shared for each professional opportunity. Applicants are also informed on vision, mission and the values that guide the company. A distinctive element is Internal Job Posting, which offers all people in Juventus the opportunity to apply for different roles, promoting internal mobility, expanding skills and professional growth in a meritocratic context.

- Networking: The Company recognises the strategic value of external collaborations to expand the talent pool and promote inclusion. With this in mind, Juventus has already started, in recent seasons, a collaboration with the CasaOz Association, through the MagazziniOz project, which supports the work integration of persons with disabilities. During the year, a position opened within our company departments, for which a selection process was initiated. Thanks to the partnership with MagazziniOz, a suitable candidate was identified who was initially appointed with a fixed-term contract. After an initial coaching

period, the person became a permanent Juventus employee, testifying to the quality of the selected profile, the effectiveness of the collaboration and the soundness of the path undertaken.

- Objective evaluation: Each open position is managed through a structured selection process, based on objective and transparent criteria. The evaluation not only focuses on technical skills, experience and qualifications, but also on the candidate's ability to integrate into the organisational environment, with the right attitude to collaborate and contribute to a positive and dynamic work environment. When possible, practical tests and business cases are proposed, which allow candidates to demonstrate their skills in realistic contexts, promoting a more complete and realistic assessment of the needs of the role. To ensure consistency, impartiality and soundness in the assessment, the cycle of interviews is generally divided into three steps, during which the candidate meets different interlocutors, with strategically increasing roles. The final decision is the result of balancing the total evaluations collected throughout the process.

- Adaptability: In a constantly evolving environment, Juventus adopts a flexible and dynamic approach, periodically updating its recruiting strategies to meet the new market needs and to align with emerging best practices. This allows the organisation to remain competitive and attractive to talent, while maintaining high quality standards in selection processes.

## REMUNERATION POLICY
(TOTAL REWARD FRAMEWORK)

The preparation, approval and implementation of the Remuneration Policy involves the following bodies and persons, each within their own sphere of competence:

- the Board of Directors;
- the Remuneration and Appointments Committee;
- the Shareholders' Meeting;
- the Board of Statutory Auditors
- the independent auditors.

In particular, the Remuneration Policy may first be submitted to the Board of Directors for approval by the Remuneration and Appointments Committee. In drawing up the Policy, the Remuneration and Appointments Committee involves the People, Culture & ESG Department, also with the aim of gathering market data in terms of practices, policies and benchmarking, ensuring regulatory compliance and improving the preparation of the same policy and, where necessary, also independent experts on the topic. Furthermore, the ESG Committee expresses its opinion on the ESG performance targets of the variable incentive schemes.

The Company has adopted a remuneration system entitled the Total Reward Framework, oriented to the needs and motivations of resources, defining a set of tools that allow to outline reward strategies tailored to and consistent with the different workforce clusters, within a single, fair and transparent structure.

More specifically, the Total Reward Framework is based on a "banding" system. The system divides company roles into eight different bands (i.e. contiguous classes of jobs) which are assessed according to Mercer's International Positioning Evaluation (IPE) method and include consistent roles in terms of responsibility, level of complexity managed and level of impact on corporate results.

The banding system is the cornerstone on which resource management, reward and development processes are built.

The Total Reward Framework consists of: (i) fixed remuneration, (ii) the STI Plan, represented by an annual short-term monetary incentive component intended, among other things, for the Chief Executive Officer and key management personnel, (iii) the LTI plan, represented by a long-term incentive component deriving from a plan based on financial instruments intended, in its first allocation cycle, for a select group of key resources, including the Chief Executive Officer and key management personnel and other employees with strategic roles within the Company or its subsidiaries; and (iv) certain benefits and ancillary services.

Both short- and long-term incentive systems include ESG KPIs within their scorecards.

Specifically with regard to the STI Plan structured with a single scorecard, consisting of three macro-targets: an economic-financial KPI, strategic KPIs for each function and an ESG KPI, as an individual target relating to environmental sustainability parameters, promotion of a sustainable culture and reduction of operating costs. In particular, the target identified for the 2024/2025 financial year (in line with the Company's ESG Strategy & Framework) is to reduce energy consumption at the Company's sites, to be assessed by comparing the energy consumption of the year of the baseline (figure as at 30 June 2024) with those at the end of the 2024/2025 financial year (as at 30 June 2025). In the STI Plan, the ESG component has a weight of 10% on total remuneration.

Also in the LTI Plan, which has a multi-year duration (until 31 December 2029) and is divided into the following three vesting periods, according to a rolling attribution logic: (i) 1 July 2024 – 30 June 2027; (ii) 1 July 2025 – 30 June 2028; and (iii) 1 July 2026 – 30 June 2029, it is envisaged in particular that the rights attributed will vest if specific economic-financial, return on shares and ESG targets are achieved. In the LTI Plan the ESG component has a weight of 15% on total remuneration with reference to the first allocation cycle and will have a weight of 10% with reference to the second allocation cycle.

The target based on the ESG KPI has been identified in obtaining and maintaining the Gender Equality Certification (PdR UNI 125/2022), introduced by the NRRP (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), the Italian plan of investments and reforms within the European Next Generation EU programme that defines the guidelines on the management system for gender equality.

The measurement of the certification is conducted at the beginning and end of the vesting period on the basis of specific qualitative and quantitative indicators and access to the certification by the certifying body is envisaged in the event that a minimum overall summary score of at least 60% is achieved.

The Total Reward Framework allows Juventus to guarantee all its resources the same work opportunities and fair salary compensation and contract terms.

## EXTERNAL COMMUNICATION GUIDELINES

As part of policies aimed at the workforce, Juventus has adopted specific Guidelines for External Communication, aimed at ensuring that any official communication is consistent with the relevant ethical and regulatory principles.

Under the responsibility of the Head of Communication, this document has been drafted in accordance with the Code of Ethics, the Organisation, Management and Control Model pursuant to Italian Legislative Decree 231/01 ('231 Model") and the Organisation, Management and Control Model pursuant to Art. 7, paragraph 5, of the FIGC Statute ('Prevention Model').

The Guidelines define the main indications relating to the Club's external communication on institutional, strategic and business topics, aimed at stakeholders such as media, institutions, federations and other public opinion subjects.

In compliance with the Code of Ethics, Juventus promotes clear, precise and truthful communication, avoiding the dissemination of information not consistent with transparency obligations and corporate strategies. This approach helps prevent reputational risks and responsibilities for the Company, and is an integral part of the responsibilities of staff authorised for external communication.

In addition, inside information is disclosed in compliance with market abuse regulations and the related corporate procedure for the management and communication of inside information.

## SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINES

In the context of internal policies aimed at the workforce, Juventus has defined and circulated the Social Media Guidelines, a document aimed at promoting the conscious, responsible and consistent use of social networks by employees and collaborators. The guidelines recognise the importance of digital communication as a means of personal expression, but also highlight the impact it can have on the Company's image and reputation.

In line with the Code of Ethics and with the values of inclusiveness and respect promoted by the Club, the Guidelines establish fundamental principles, including:

- individual responsibility in the publication of content,
- the need to distinguish personal opinions from official Club positions;
- compliance with privacy, intellectual property and

copyright regulations;

- the prohibition on publishing discriminatory content or content harmful to the reputation of the Company's or its stakeholders.

Under the responsibility of the People, Culture & ESG Chief, the Guidelines also promote inclusiveness as a central value, encouraging respectful and diversity-conscious communication, and provide practical guidelines for the safe and professional use of social platforms.

The adoption of these guidelines is part of the broader People & Culture policy framework, with the target of protecting workers, enhancing their role as brand ambassadors, and ensuring a positive digital environment that complies with ethical and legal standards.

## HEALTH AND SAFETY POLICY

Juventus has adopted a **Health and Safety Management System** ("HSMS"), according to the ISO 45001:2018 international standard, achieving its first certification on 25 September 2009 (on the then available OHSAS 18001:2007). With a view to continuous improvement of the health and safety levels of workers, the system is audited by the Certifying Body on an annual basis. Following a third-party audit, the Body renews the certificate (last confirmation of the certification: 19-21-24 September 2024).

Training is provided in compliance with the agreements of the State-Regions Conference in force; the main prevention and protection measures are the implementation of information and, where necessary, training also on process topics (e.g. procedures), participation in annual emergency tests, maintenance of plant health and safety conditions, equipment and facilities. These measures seek to make people aware of health and safety issues and safe behaviour during work activities. In particular, through the **Occupational Health and Safety Policy** developed in the procedures and instructions of the HSMS, which allow compliance with Italian Legislative Decree 81/08, under the responsibility of the Employer.

Since maintenance activities are outsourced to some main contractors, a specific topic concerns contracts, which are managed in compliance with Article 26 or, in the case of construction interventions, with Title IV of Italian Legislative Decree 81/08.

## QUALITY POLICY FOR THE MEDICAL SECTOR

Not only to achieve its football objectives, but also for the well-being of its employees, Juventus ensures that its athletes and technical staff are in the best possible mental, physical and working conditions. Due to the particular nature of its business, the players' working conditions are a key aspect for the Club. In this sense, Juventus is committed to offering, through innovative structures such as J Medical, the JTCC and the JTCV, the best **medical-sporting, nutritional and psychological facilities** in order to guarantee the highest possible performance levels. Juventus certifies the achievement of these quality standards also through the implementation of its **quality policy for the medical sector**, which defines the guidelines and targets for protecting the players and the technical sector, under the supervision

of the health officer. The Club's medical sector has a **certified ISO 9001:2015** Quality Management System, whose purpose is to protect the health management of players by the Juventus medical sector in both preventive and therapeutic terms.

## SAFEGUARDING POLICY

Juventus has developed a **Safeguarding Policy**, with the aim of ensuring the protection of its registered players and technical staff, particularly those underage. For further information on the targets, scope and purposes, please refer to section G1-1 – "Corporate culture and business conduct policies".

## S1-2 – PROCESSES FOR ENGAGING WITH OWN WORKERS AND WORKERS' REPRESENTATIVES ABOUT IMPACTS

Juventus adopts a wide variety of channels to directly interact with its people, regarding the material impacts affecting them. The activities described below aim to identify, manage and remediate any impacts that the Club may cause in relation to its people. Coordinated by the *People, Culture & ESG Department*, employee engagement activities have modalities that may vary from formal consultations to informal meetings, ensuring that each person has the opportunity to express their opinion. This approach derives from the ESG Strategy outlined for employees in the "People First" pillar that focuses on people within the Club. The pillar underlines Juventus' commitment to integrating ESG topics into every aspect of its activities, whether or not they are related to sport, while ensuring virtuous development, engagement and well-being paths for all people.

The **onboarding programme** for all new resources who become part of Juventus plays a central role in the people engagement process framework.

The Club has developed a structured and articulated onboarding plan, designed to effectively welcome new employees, promoting their transition and accelerate the professional integration process. The target is to ensure a positive, productive and conscious start in the new role, fostering a sense of belonging and engagement from the outset.

The plan consists of a series of training activities and opportunities that embrace several fundamental aspects:

- **Welcome:** From the first day, the new employee is engagingly welcomed, is introduced to colleagues and team members, is guided through the company spaces, receive a Welcome Kit and share practical information useful to orient themselves within the new working environment. The Welcome Kit includes the official Men's First Team strip, personalised with the name of the new employee and the year of appointment, a backpack, a canteen and gadgets essential for business life. This initial moment is designed to create a positive and reassuring climate, promoting a peaceful and gradual inclusion;

- **Training:** Targeted and specific training is provided, calibrated on the role and responsibilities assigned. The training includes both technical content related to the job, and transversal elements relating to business processes, internal policies, health and safety in the workplace principles, and initiatives to support people's well-being. The target is to provide all the necessary tools to operate effectively and consciously right from the start;

- **Organisational orientation:** The structure of the organisation is illustrated, with an overview of the key departments and functions. This helps the new employee understand their role within the company system and identify the main interlocutors they need to collaborate with.

- **Targets and expectations:** From the early stages, the Manager explains to the individual their targets and performance expectations, already outlined during the selection process. This allows the new resource to have a clear vision of the responsibilities and milestones to be achieved, fostering a structured and measurable growth path.

The plan consists of the following sections:

# 1. Corporate Induction

This phase is dedicated to providing an overview of the organisation and facilitating integration into the Company environment, and it includes:

- Health & Safety Training: in compliance with current regulations, specific information and training on health and safety topics in the workplace is provided to ensure a safe environment for people and compliance with expected regulatory standards.

# 2. Individual Induction

This phase is customised according to the role and specific characteristics of the position. The new resource takes part in individual or team meetings with the main stakeholders they will collaborate with, with the target of building effective professional relationships from the start and understanding the operational dynamics of their area of reference. This approach promotes smooth and natural integration into the workplace, avoiding the discomfort of having to contact unknown interlocutors to manage operational activities, and offering clear and accessible points of reference right from the start.

For each of the tools indicated above, the Company is able to carry out appropriate monitoring in order to ensure and verify the engagement effectiveness.

The People First Policy helps the organisation better understand the perspectives of workers who may be particularly vulnerable to impacts or marginalised through a structured approach that values diversity and guarantees equal opportunities. The principles of fairness, inclusion, accessibility and enhancement of

the differences referred to in the Policy actually drive the specific needs of these groups to be taken into consideration in internal decisions and processes. For example, the adoption of inclusive recruitment practices and the promotion of gender equality – strengthened by the achievement of the UNI/PdR 125/2022 certification, together with training and awareness-raising courses, contribute to enhance the different perspectives, reducing the risks of exclusion and discrimination. In this regard, an ESG Steering Committee was established to ensure the correct Policy application.

# S1-3 – PROCESSES TO REMEDIATE NEGATIVE IMPACTS AND CHANNELS FOR OWN WORKERS TO RAISE CONCERNS

Juventus has established dedicated channels to allow its employees to directly report needs or concerns. To this end, Juventus provides them with a reporting channel, accessible on-line at the public address: https://juventus.segnalazioni.net/ dedicated and secure, through which it is possible to report breaches of company laws, regulations, procedures and policies or to report, more generally, situations of potential risk.

This system protects the identity of the whistleblowers and guarantees the confidentiality of reports, which are visible only to the Whistleblowing Committee ("Whistleblowing Committee"), which handles them in accordance with the principles of impartiality and confidentiality. In addition, the Company has put in place strict measures to prevent any form of retaliation against those reporting through the channel. Juventus prohibits such acts, whether direct or indirect, against the whistleblower, and envisages disciplinary sanctions against anyone who violates this prohibition or the obligations to protect the confidentiality of the whistleblower's identity.

In order to increase awareness of this channel availability, employees receive training on compliance topics, including those relating to the reporting process through the whistleblowing platform. These training opportunities are part of the company's onboarding plan, for which reference is made to sections S1-2 – "Processes for engaging with own workers and workers' representatives about impacts" and S1-13 – "Training and skills development metrics".

For further details, please refer to section G1-1 – "Corporate culture and business conduct policies (Whistleblowing Management)".

# S1-4 – TAKING ACTION ON MATERIAL IMPACTS ON OWN WORKFORCE, AND APPROACHES TO MITIGATING MATERIAL RISKS AND PURSUING MATERIAL OPPORTUNITIES RELATED TO OWN WORKFORCE, AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THOSE ACTIONS

Juventus is constantly committed to managing impacts on its own workforce, highlighting both risks and opportunities. In this regard, the Club has implemented actions and initiatives aimed at fostering people's mental and physical well-being, engagement, a sense of belonging and sharing among its employees. In a corporate context increasingly oriented towards the well-being and enhancement of staff, the Club stands out for its strong commitment to creating opportunities that not only strengthen the link between collaborators and the Club, but also contribute to building a cohesive and motivated community.

The management of issues related to its own workforce involves different areas of business, in particular the People, Culture & ESG Department, composed of 17 people, who, with the support of specific functions, collaborate to continuously monitor and improve the work environment, promoting training, enhancement of talent and protection of employees' rights.

# HEALTH AND SAFETY

Over the years, Juventus has adopted a structured management system and a set of processes and actions to mitigate potential negative impacts on the health and safety of all employees through a HSMS, compliant with the ISO 45001:2018 international standard.

For further information, please refer to section S1-1 – "Policies related to own workforce".

paying particular attention to health, prevention and emotional and relational support. The approach adopted has aimed to create a work environment that is increasingly attentive to individual needs, promoting initiatives that can generate value for both people and the organisation.

In keeping with its constant commitment to ensuring the well-being of its staff, the companies continues to actively promote remote work as a strategic tool to combine productivity and work-life balance. In fact, remote work not only improves the quality of life of workers by reducing commuting stress and increasing freedom in time management, but also represents a concrete lever for environmental sustainability. Reducing daily commuting results in lower CO₂ emissions, with a positive impact on our ecological footprint, even if we consider the additional consumption related to remote working.

Remote work is thus confirmed as a win-win solution for all parties involved: it improves individual well-being, supports productivity and strengthens the Company's commitment to a more sustainable and responsible future.

In view of the expiry of the Company Regulation on remote work scheduled for 30 June 2025, the Club has a new regulation with all its people, aimed at simplifying access to this working mode. Although the total number of days available is unchanged, the new structure now allows a more flexible and continuous use of remote work so as to more effectively meet personal and family needs.

In addition to remote work, one of the most material activities is 'Health Talks', a series of information webinars aimed at increasing awareness on health and prevention issues. In particular, topics related to skin care and female health were explored with the contribution of industry experts.

An internal survey was conducted on World Mental Health Day with the aim of exploring people's views on mental health in the company. The survey made it possible to gather concrete ideas on the areas of greatest interest, current perceptions and initiatives to be activated, also laying the foundations for a future structured on listening to the organisational climate.

Based on the feedback received, T.E.A.M. Strength – Tools for Empowerment And Mental Strength was designed, a project created to concretely respond to the needs expressed.

The process was developed through three in-person meetings, each one addressing a key issue for mental

health and the development of relational and personal skills:

- Stress management through mindfulness: a strong need has been identified for practical tools to address daily pressures. Simple and accessible mindfulness techniques were then shared, with the aim of promoting mindfulness, improving focus and developing greater emotional resilience.
- Value of intergenerational factors in working environments: dialogue between different generations has been recognised as a valuable resource. Promoting intergenerational exchange means not only transmitting know-how and experiences, but also creating authentic connections, breaking down stereotypes and promoting a more inclusive and collaborative culture.
- Mutual recognition as a lever for the awareness and quality of professional relationships: the need to feel seen, listened to and valued has been clearly identified. Recognition was understood as an authentic act, going beyond simple formal approval, contributing to countering the risk of 'false consent' and nurturing relationships based on trust, transparency and mutual respect.

The meetings were led by Prof. Giuseppe Vercelli's team, responsible for Juventus' psychological well-being, and offered authentic opportunities for dialogue and practical tools to be applied in daily functions. Registration was optional, but required participation in the entire cycle, at the end of which a certificate of participation was issued.

Again with a view to mental and physical well-being, the Sport Programme, the programme dedicated to the mental and physical well-being of people which continued also into the 2024/2025 season, is also included, offering the opportunity to practice Pilates, Functional Training and Yoga at JHQ during lunch breaks.

The Fitness Room opened in 2024, realised in collaboration with the Technogym partner, continues to represent an invaluable space where to train, regenerate and find work-life balance. In addition, the Sport Programme has been expanded at the JTCV, allowing employees to also use the gym normally reserved exclusively for youth teams, thus promoting greater engagement and the opportunity of being involved in physical activities in a professional and stimulating environment.

# ATTENTION TO PEOPLE REPRESENTS A STRATEGIC PILLAR FOR THE COMPANY, WHICH RECOGNISES THAT THE QUALITY OF WORK EXPERIENCE DIRECTLY AFFECTS THE MOTIVATION, PERFORMANCE AND OVERALL SUSTAINABILITY OF THE WORK ENVIRONMENT.

With this in mind, Juventus has continued to develop innovative programs aimed at fostering the balance between professional and personal life, physical and mental health, sustainable mobility and the sense of belonging of its business community.

Below is a summary of the main initiatives made available during the season:

# CULTURE, CONDUCT AND AWARENESS

Juventus considers it essential to promote ethical and correct behaviour consistent with its values, especially in relation to the conduct of players, collaborators and all people operating within the Club. To strengthen this culture, a series of cross-cutting actions were activated involving formal training as well as awareness-raising and engagement.

In particular, the professional players - male and female players - receive **dedicated training**, provided directly by the **Risk & Compliance and Internal Audit Directorate**, aimed at ensuring full awareness of the rules and expected behaviour. The contents covered include the **Club Code of Ethics** (no 231 Model, the **Prevention Model** and, more generally, awareness raising towards issues related to behaviour contrary to the **Sports Justice Code** and principles of loyalty, fairness and probity, with

the aim of providing concrete tools to guide individual conduct. The activity is carried out systematically and detailed and is an integral part of the broader **compliance induction programme** envisaged for all new resources. For further information, please refer to section S-13 – "Training metrics".

During the season, a training course was provided for Line Data Managers and Referents aimed at strengthening skills in the area of privacy and empowerment on the data processed for data protection purposes ("Data Protection"). The training provided a regulatory update and concerned, in particular, the use of the CORA application, a tool adopted by the Company for processing tracing and management pursuant to the regulations on personal data protection. The aim of the initiative was to ensure greater awareness, monitoring and correctness in the processes of information collection and use, to protect people and the organisation.

In parallel with these initiatives, Juventus continues to invest in building a solid and responsible corporate culture based on respect, responsibility and inclusion. During the 2024/2025 season, the Club took a significant step in this direction, defining and sharing the new Purpose, Values & Behaviours, identity pillars that guide daily behaviour and choices within the organisation. The dissemination process was accompanied by opportunities for discussion aimed at fostering the active involvement of people and stimulating a deep understanding of new cultural references.

To support this path, Juventus has activated a series of targeted training interventions, developed in collaboration with specialised partners, on topics with high social and cultural impact. Of these projects:

- the prevention of gender-based violence and discriminatory language, through a process carried out with Fondazione Libellula, aimed at promoting a safe, respectful and conscious working environment;
- contrasting cyberbullying and risks related to sharpening, thanks to the collaboration with Fondazione Carolina, with a particular focus on digital implications concerning the youth and family world;
- the prevention of abuse and inequalities in sport, with the support of Change The Game, to promote an inclusive, fair and responsible sports culture;
- the launch of the AWorld app, an interactive platform designed to stimulate individual and collective engagement on issues related to sustainability and conscious lifestyles.

To consciously and responsibly monitor the communication sphere, Juventus has introduced specific tools to guide behaviour and promote a consistent and respectful use of information channels. Among these, the Social Media Guidelines for all staff offer clear indications on the use of digital channels in professional and personal contexts, while the Guidelines for External Communication, dedicated to the Club's public speakers, support the management of public relations in line with the Company's identity, values and positioning.

Through these initiatives, in line with the strategic "People First" pillar, Juventus reinforces its commitment to creating a work environment where every person feels an active part of a community that shares values, objectives and a broader path for **integrating sustainability into the Club culture and in all its components**.

# S1-5 – TARGETS RELATED TO MANAGING MATERIAL NEGATIVE IMPACTS, ADVANCING POSITIVE IMPACTS, AND MANAGING MATERIAL RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES

The IRDs related to workforce management are focused on some strategic areas that directly affect sustainability and the quality of the work environment. In particular, Juventus pays attention to four priority areas:

- Health and mental and physical well-being: promoting a general state of well-being, promoting balance, prevention and care, is essential to ensure sustainable and resilient working conditions;
- People's satisfaction and engagement: the level of internal engagement is a key indicator of the organisation's cultural vitality and its ability to generate a sense of belonging and motivation;
- Talent attraction and retention: the ability to attract, develop and retain quality professionalism is closely linked to the company climate, the development and orientation of the leadership and the effectiveness of people development policies.
- Diversity, equity and inclusion: promoting a working environment that values differences, guarantees equal opportunities and stimulates the authentic expression of each person is an essential lever for innovation and organisational cohesion.

# PEOPLE'S WELL-BEING AND SATISFACTION ARE STRATEGIC LEVERS FOR THE SUSTAINABLE GROWTH OF THE ORGANISATION

and, for this reason, have been formally integrated into the targets of the 2025/2026 STI Plan. In particular, a specific KPI was introduced aimed at enhancing the dissemination of the culture of well-being through the active participation of the plan's recipients in business initiatives dedicated to physical, mental and preventive well-being.

The direct involvement of the Leadership Team, which will take on an active role in promoting virtuous behaviour and consolidating a culture of general and organisation-wide well-being, is envisaged to strengthen the initiative's effectiveness.

# KPI details - 2025/2026 STI

To achieve the target, documented participation in at least one activity in each of the following categories is required:

- Physical activity (e.g. corporate sports programmes, use of the internal gym).
- Training on health, mental well-being or prevention (e.g. workshops, seminars or dedicated information programmes).

## S1-6 – CHARACTERISTICS OF THE UNDERTAKING'S EMPLOYEES

For the purposes of the S1-6 principle, the table provides a detailed overview of the main contractual types that make up Juventus's workforce, divided into two areas: **sports staff** and **corporate staff**. This distinction is functional to understand the variety of roles and contractual forms that characterise a structured football organisation such as Juventus.

### SPORTS STAFF

Sports staff include:

- **Employee S1-6**, hired under a subordinated contract pursuant to Italian Legislative Decree 36/2021 for sports work. This category includes **professional players**, **sports managers**, **coaches** and **athletics trainers**. The definition of the S1-6 indicator also includes **players with an apprenticeship contract** (a case in point envisaged starting from the 2023/2024 season).

- **Non-employees S1-7**, involved through:

- **Coordinated and Continuous Collaboration contracts** (coaches, observers, athletic trainers, massage therapists and other staff figures) who operate on a para-subordinate and non-continuous basis or if there is a prevalent subordinate employment in place with a third party;
- **Self-employed professionals (VAT-registered)** Type chosen in the presence of specific professions and specialisations that routinely operate on an autonomous basis also through registrations in Professional Registers (e.g. doctors, physiotherapists, etc.).

**Note:** The category 'non-professional players' includes young players in the youth teams, for whom an apprenticeship or professional player contract has not been stipulated. Juventus also provides disclosure on this component, although it is aware that, as they are not workers in the strict sense, they do not fall within the notion of 'workforce' within the more traditional sense. However, their inclusion reflects the Club's desire to represent all those involved in its sports ecosystems in a transparent and complete manner, also in view of the significant number of registered players and technical staff and the potential educational and training impact on them.

### CORPORATE STAFF

Corporate staff include:

- **Employees S1-6**, divided into **Executive Managers**, to whom the National Collective Bargaining Agreement for Executives employed in Goods and Services Companies applies, and **middle managers**, **office staff** and **manual workers**, governed by internal company regulations
- **Non-employees S1-7**, as extra-curricular trainees for a period of at least 6 months and steward staff, occasional employees pursuant to Article 54 bis of Italian Decree-Law no. 50 of 24 April 2017, as subsequently amended

This staff composition reflects a corporate workforce structured according to traditional models, but enhanced by the presence of temporary and support figures, who contribute to operational needs in a flexible and targeted manner.

Overall,

**JUVENTUS' WORKFORCE REFLECTS THE ORGANISATIONAL COMPLEXITY OF A LARGE FOOTBALL CLUB, IN WHICH DIVERSE SPORTING AND PROFESSIONAL SKILLS COEXIST.**

The presence of different types of contracts meets the need to adapt the employment structure to the specific characteristics of roles, the duration of services and the nature of activities, while ensuring operational flexibility and compliance with industry regulations.

The analysis of data relating to staff breakdown by gender shows a marked male prevalence. This imbalance is attributable to the specific and historical characteristics of the football sector, which has traditionally seen a strong male presence, particularly in technical and sports roles. This trend reflects a long-term consolidated context, consolidated at both national and international level, in which female participation has historically been limited, especially in operational areas directly related to sports performance.

In particular, the technical and support staff – such as

coaches, athletic trainers and similar figures – is still largely composed of men today, testifying to a cultural and professional approach that is only recently starting to evolve.

This situation is not an expression of exclusive or discriminatory choices by Juventus, but rather represents a realistic reflection of the labour market in football. However, the Club is aware of the need to foster structural change and, with this in mind, has started a progressive selection and recruitment standardisation process within the Football area. The adoption of more objective

## METHODOLOGICAL NOTE

The outgoing turnover rate was calculated as the ratio of the number of employees leaving the company to the number of total employees as at 30 June 2025; in particular:

- With regard to the denominator: the staff figures are taken into account as at 30 June 2025 (the end of the 24/25 sport season).
- With regard to the numerator: all outgoing staff during the 2024/2025 season were taken into account; the people who have terminated their employment on 30 June 2025 are still included on that date as the effecti-

ve exit date is 1 July 2025.

- The figures for incoming and outgoing staff are influenced by the seasonality of the sports staff contracts which provide for termination at the end of the season (30 June) and possible subsequent re-hiring.

To offer a more stable representation of the company in terms of its stable component, Juventus has, therefore, developed a second table referring exclusively to corporate staff. In this context, the turnover rate is significantly lower, reflecting greater employment continuity and a lower degree of mobility.

## S1-7 – CHARACTERISTICS OF NON-EMPLOYEES IN THE UNDERTAKING'S OWN WORKFORCE

As indicated in the previous section, Juventus' non-employees include professionals categorised as Coordinated and Continuous Collaborations (coaches, observers, athletic trainers and massage therapists), those with a VAT number (medical staff), trainees and stewards.

This classification reflects the different operational needs of the sports structure, where professionals with full-time roles and specialists coexist with more flexible collaborations.

On the other hand, below is a detailed analysis of another category of non-employees, namely **Stewards**. In accordance with the provisions of the **Decree of the Italian Minister of the Interior**, as well as of the **directives of the FIGC and Lega Serie A**, Juventus implements a structured **stewarding** system to ensure events take place in order, security and reception conditions. Stewards perform key tasks, including:

- public welcome and orientation,
- control and safety,
- spectators assistance,
- emergency management.

Stewards are **categorised as occasional employees** pursuant to Article 54 bis of Italian Decree-Law no. 50 of 24 April 2017, as subsequently amended, and, therefore, as **non-employees** in accordance with the ESRS S1-7 disclosure requirement.

The following information relating to the workforce employed in stewarding activities for the 2024/2025 season is reported below:

- **Total number of stewards trained and contactable** as at 30 June 2025: 859. This figure reflects the number of persons who have confirmed their availability for the 2024/2025 season. Juventus proceeds with a request for availability for each individual event about 10 days before the match and, depending on the personal availability, collaborators confirm or decline their presence.

- Every steward participated in a **compulsory training course** that includes theoretical and practical modules on safety standards, emergency management and interaction with the public.

- Two teams dedicated to persons with disabilities in the North and South sectors, respectively, led by a supervisor. The steward courses organised by Juventus - as a training body accredited by ONMS (National Observatory on Sports Events)

- includes two hours' training in LIS (Italian Sign Language).
- **Average number of stewards active per event** at Allianz Stadium: 530. This value varies according to the criticality of the match, according to assessments made before each match.
- Before each event, **A pre-match briefing** takes place before each event, with all stewards participating to receive updates on specific operating procedures, evacuation plans and coordination with public order forces.

These activities are a key element in the responsible management of sports events, ensuring a controlled and safe environment for all participants.

### S1-9 – DIVERSITY METRICS

Juventus carefully monitors the composition of its own workforce in relation to key variables linked to diversity, with particular reference to gender and age groups. The following tables offer a summary representation of staff's demographic profile as at 30 June 2025, with a specific focus on Top Management ("Top Management") and distribution by demographic ranges.

The data shows a prevalence of men within Top Management (66.7%) compared to women (33.3%). This reflects once again the characteristics of the football and sports sector in which the Club operates, historically characterised by male dominance in top management roles, while recognising the importance of promoting greater inclusion also at this level. Juventus is working to strengthen the presence of women in strategic roles, including through internal development paths and activities aimed at enhancing female talent.

This commitment to fairness was formally recognised with the UNI/PdR 125:2022 Gender Equality Certification, which testifies to the Club's willingness to adopt concrete policies and measures to promote a fair, inclusive and talent-oriented work environment. The analysis conducted during the certification process also highlighted areas for improvement, including the increase in women's representation in top management roles, a key element for an increasingly balanced and representative governance.

This is the direction towards which Juventus's willingness to develop and implement a structured Career Development Framework by the 2025/2026 season is developing, with the aim of making the professional growth process within the organisation transparent, accessible and meritocratic. The framework aims to support people in understanding and managing their development path, while promoting the identification and enhancement of talent in line with the Club's strategic objectives.

Specifically, the Career Development Framework will include:

- the definition of a clear policy that describes criteria, steps and tools useful for professional growth, making the path understandable and accessible to all;
- the active involvement of the management and Leadership Team in promoting a culture of growth and widespread responsibility;
- the supervision of fairness and consistency in evaluation and progress criteria, guaranteeing inclusiveness and meritocracy.

Distribution by age group shows a balanced and diversified structure: 48% of staff fall within the 30 to 50 years range, with under 30s accounting for 34% over 50s for 18%. This composition reflects a dynamic workforce, in which junior and senior profiles coexist, contributing to a rich and stimulating generational mix.

## S1-10 – ADEQUATE WAGES

Regardless of gender or contract type, Juventus guarantees employees entry wages at least equal to the minimum established by law or applicable collective bargaining agreements. This approach reflects the Club's commitment to promoting pay equity and the building of a work environment based on transparency, meritocracy, and social justice criteria. Wages adequacy is also constantly monitored in relation to the relevant market, in order to enhance internal skills and support workers' economic well-being throughout their professional career.

With this in mind, Juventus has adopted a structured *Total Reward Framework*, which is the basis for consistent and strategic management of remuneration policies. The system consists of:

- a fixed remuneration;
- a short-term variable component (STI Plan), linked to the achievement of annual targets;
- a long-term variable component (LTI Plan), based on financial instruments and intended for corporate Top Management;
- benefit and ancillary services to support employee well-being.

The Total Reward Framework is based on a banding system, a methodology that allows the value generated

by each professional position within the organisation to be assessed. This approach makes it possible to ensure internal fairness, ensuring consistency between responsibility, expected contribution and economic treatment, and at the same time to maintain a high level of external competitiveness, thanks to constant alignment with market benchmarks.

Through this model, Juventus strengthens its commitment to an organisational culture oriented towards the enhancement of merit, transparency in decision-making processes and the sustainable development of its resources, in line with the Corporate Remuneration Policy and the Club's long-term objectives.

It should be noted that the transposition of the EU Directive 2023/970 on remuneration transparency by the Member States is planned by June 2026. Juventus has already started the analyses and activities necessary for readiness for the entry into force of the aforementioned legislation.

# S1-12 – PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES

The inclusion of persons with disabilities represents a concrete commitment for Juventus, oriented not only towards compliance with regulations, but towards the creation of shared value and real opportunities. Each appointment takes place starting from a real business need and is based on the careful assessment of the person's skills, individual possibilities and operational needs, with the aim of making an effective and sustainable matching for both parties.

This approach is also made possible thanks to virtuous relationships with local organisations, such as Casa Oz and Magazzini Oz, which work to support the work

inclusion of persons with physical and intellectual disabilities, promoting conscious, personalised and well-accompanied integration paths.

Confirming the soundness of this model, at the end of the 2024/2025 season a position in the corporate area was converted into an open-ended contract, the second in the last two years.

This is a result that demonstrates how the integration paths initiated translate into stable and valuable opportunities, both for those involved and for the reference teams, representing a concrete example of how inclusion can turn into a lasting resource, contributing to the building of a fairer, collaborative and diversity-conscious working environment.

# S1-13 – TRAINING AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT METRICS

In terms of training and development, Juventus continues to view training as a fundamental lever in supporting the Club's business strategy. As stated in the Code of Ethics, the Company pays particular attention to aspects related to the training of in-house staff and newly appointed employees, which are integrated into the broader human resources management system. Annually, a training plan is developed for all Club employees offering ongoing training initiatives, including through external resources and platforms.

In continuity with the previous season, during the 2024/2025 season the corporate strategy continued to enhance the training and development of people, in line with organisational priorities, the business strategy and the principles of equity, inclusion and managerial growth.

# Upskilling & Continuous learning

To respond promptly to the training needs of the entire company population,

# A BOTTOM-UP APPROACH WAS ADOPTED FOR THE FIRST TIME, CONSIDERED MORE EFFECTIVE THAN TRAINING IMPOSED FROM ABOVE.

With this in mind, a structured collection of training needs was carried out, actively involving the People Managers ('People Manager') of all company areas. This method made it possible to enhance the various functions' views, ensuring greater correspondence of the training offer with the real operational and development needs of people. The proposals that emerged were subsequently analysed and harmonised into an integrated training plan, divided into three main clusters:

- Hard Skills - development of advanced operational capabilities and sectoral know-how.
- Soft Skills - strengthening of transversal skills such as emotional intelligence, effective communication

![img-114.jpeg](img-114.jpeg)

and inclusive leadership.

- Well-being - promoting a healthy and sustainable working environment, with a focus on individual and collective well-being.

The target is to offer diversified and accessible opportunities to the entire corporate population, in line with real operational and strategic priorities.

# Hard Skills

AI Skills Boost | During the 2024/2025 season, Juventus started a structured and progressive process to introduce Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a strategic lever for transformation and innovation within the organisation. This path was not limited to providing technical concepts, but intended to promote a corporate culture capable of consciously integrating AI into daily processes, enhancing its potential in terms of efficiency, quality and predictive capacity.

The initiative consisted of two main phases:

- Am (AI Smart): an introductory phase intended for the entire corporate population, aimed at fostering an understanding of fundamental AI concepts, its cross-cutting applications and the benefits it can generate in the workplace. The aim was not only informative, but also cultural: to raise people's awareness of AI opportunities and stimulate critical and conscious reflection on its use.
- AI Evolution: a pilot project launched subsequently, involving 50 people selected on a voluntary basis from all company departments, with the aim of directly testing the adoption of AI in real scenarios. The group worked on optimising internal processes through intelligent tools and solutions, with a view to concrete

and measurable innovation. The project represents a first operational experimentation with the integration of AI into organisational models, and is the basis for a future larger extension on a company scale.

The adoption of AI was conceived not as a simple technological update, but as a cultural shift that requires new skills, an open mindset and a collaborative approach to innovation. To this end, further training occasions and opportunities for discussion are provided to accompany people towards a conscious and responsible transition, capable of ensuring a sustainable evolution of roles and working methods.

Language Development | During the season, Juventus also launched a new project to promote language development as a lever for inclusion, personal growth and international collaboration. We have chosen to make available to all our people the GoFluent platform, which allows the learning of 19 of the most spoken and strategic languages in the world, meeting the different professional needs, in addition to just English. The path starts with an individual assessment of the starting level, and then proposes customised content, exercises and conversation classes structured by thematic area and knowledge level. The project also envisages the possibility of extending access to a loved person, strengthening the link between individual well-being and family dimension. To encourage the use of the platform, a gamification mechanism was introduced towards the end of the season, which awarded the most active participants with individual lessons with native speakers, encouraging continuous learning in a motivating and inclusive manner.

Based on the principles of emotional intelligence, the programme is a veritable training in managerial skills,

# Talent Management Programme

During the 2024/2025 season, Juventus launched the second edition of the Talent Management Programme ("TMP"), consolidating its commitment to the enhancement and development of high potential people within the organisation.

The initiative is confirmed within a broader internal growth strategy, with the aim of accompanying talents in their journey and contributing to building a culture oriented towards continuous development and widespread leadership.

The programme involved 16 participants from all company departments, selected through a careful process intended to recognise the potential expressed in the professional context, while ensuring a balanced representation in terms of gender, functions and organisational levels.

The path consists of five strategic guidelines, designed to accompany the talents in a personal and profession growth experience:

ASSESSMENT

COACHING

EDUCATION

![img-116.jpeg](img-116.jpeg)

MENTORING

![img-117.jpeg](img-117.jpeg)

CAREER DEVELOPMENT

# FIVE STRATEGIC PILLARS

- Assessment: the participants took part in a structured journey to explore their professional and managerial style, with the aim of developing greater self-awareness of their working identity. Through internationally recognised tools – such as the Public Identity 360° and the Hogan Assessment – it has been possible to analyse in depth the perception that others have of one's own contribution, the distinctive skills and the main areas of development, promoting a concrete and growth-oriented reflection.
- Coaching: based on their assessment results, each

talent has undertaken an individual coaching path, designed to strengthen managerial skills, promote self-effectiveness and strengthen orientation towards growth and change.

- Education: Juventus has made available an individual training budget for the independent choice of learning paths, with a focus on hard and soft skills. The main areas of interest focused on leadership, language development, negotiation and digital skills, confirming the importance of customising the training experience.

# ESG TRAINING AND ACTIVE ENGAGEMENT WITH THE AWORLD PLATFORM

During the 2024/2025 season, Juventus launched a collaboration with AWorld, an internationally recognised platform (awarded by Google as "Best app for good" in 2023) and chosen by the United Nations to support the ActNow campaign and by the European Commission for Climate Pact. The aim was to promote greater awareness among employees of environmental and social sustainability issues through an interactive, accessible and engaging training experience.

AWorld is a digital "Sustainability People Engagement" platform based on gamification logic, which allows the learning of the key principles of the 2030 Agenda and, more generally, sustainability. Through quizzes, training content ("stories"), suggestions for virtuous behaviour and the monitoring of their daily actions (such as sustainable mobility or energy saving), each participant was called upon to act responsibly and become part of the change.

Juventus has created a dedicated company community, where all employees are invited to take an active part. An internal classification was updated every month, symbolically rewarding the most active collaborators, thus strengthening team spirit and collective participation.

The initiative was an innovative way to integrate ESG training into staff growth paths, incentivising concrete and daily sustainable behaviour, in line with the principles of the "People First" pillar and in line with the

Black, White & More strategy. Thanks to its experience with AWorld, Juventus has strengthened its corporate culture on environmental impact, social ethics and individual responsibility issues.

# YOUTH SECTOR TRAINING – PURPOSE, VALUES AND BEHAVIOURS PROJECT

In the 2024/2025 season, the entire youth sector was involved in an important training initiative related to the Purpose, Values and Behaviours project, launched by the Company on 1 November 2024, on the occasion of the anniversary of the Club's founding. All children and young people from the youth sectors were invited to participate in a workshop at Allianz Stadium, where they were able to represent and absorb the values and behaviours that Juventus promotes and embodies.

This activity involved more than 400 people including young players and their technical staff.

This initiative has represented a fundamental point for collective growth and cultural consolidation within the youth sectors.

# COMPLIANCE AND HEALTH & SAFETY

Also for the 2024/2025 season, Juventus reaffirms the centrality of compliance as a key element of its organisational culture. The commitment is not limited to Health & Safety, but also extends to full compliance with regulations on corporate responsibility, to protect the integrity and sustainability of the work environment.

For further details, please refer to section G1-1 – "Corporate culture and business conduct policies".

## S1-14 – HEALTH AND SAFETY METRICS

All Juventus employees are covered by the HSMS, in accordance with the international UNI ISO 45001:2018 standard. This system is:

- subject to periodic internal audit;
- subject to external audit by an independent third party;
- formally certified.

The management system activities include risk assessment, periodic training, internal inspection activities aimed at compliance with mandatory regulations, achieving higher standards, and the ability to be comparable when necessary, with the principles of the

main control bodies (in particular, Work Inspectorate and the Prevention and safety service in the workplace (SPreSAL) of ASI, Piemonte). The following were recorded during the 2024/2025 season:

- 0 work-related injuries for employees;
- 0 deaths;
- 0 serious injuries;
- 0 working days lost due to injuries;
- 0 injuries during work-related or business travel.

Finally, there were no documented cases of occupational disease during the period considered.

# S1-16 – REMUNERATION METRICS (PAY GAP AND TOTAL REMUNERATION)

Gross hourly pay indicates the average earnings per hour worked, calculated by contract category (executive managers, middle managers, office staff and manual workers) and broken down by gender, indicating the gender pay gap within each category.

|  Gross hourly pay | 2024/2025 Season  |   |   |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|   |  M | W | Gap  |
|  Executive managers | 113.12 | 80.78 | 28.59%  |

# METHODOLOGICAL NOTE

The analysis was conducted exclusively on corporate staff, i.e. executive managers categorised according to the National Collective Bargaining Agreement for Executives employed in Goods and Services Companies, middle managers, office staff and manual workers$^{10}$. In fact, these are the sole categories for which work was organised on an hourly basis. Sports staff, whose contractual classification does not provide for an hourly structure similar to that of office staff and follows specific market logic, were excluded from the sports staff perimeter. In this way, the data shows a clear and comparable picture of the remuneration dynamics within the corporate component of the Club.

The total compensation ratio measures the ratio of the highest individual annual remuneration to the total annual remuneration of the median employee (excluding the highest paid). In Juventus' case, as this is a football club, the ratio is particularly broad. This value is determined by the fact that the highest remuneration corresponds to that of a professional player, whose remuneration follows specific market logics and is not comparable with those applied to corporate staff. In fact, the median remuneration includes both the remuneration of the sports part (which also include players with significantly higher remuneration levels) and that of corporate employees, who are instead on values in line with the relevant labour market.

# S1-17 – INCIDENTS, COMPLAINTS AND SEVERE HUMAN RIGHTS IMPACTS

Juventus recognises the importance of its role in condemning any human rights violations and works to prevent violence/molestation incidents occurring within its perimeter. During the reporting period, Juventus recorded no serious incidents, formal complaints or public reports related to human rights violations linked to its own workforce. In particular, no cases of discrimination, harassment or other serious negative impacts were identified, such as to require sanctions, compensation or extraordinary corrective actions.

The Club recognises correct whistleblowing practice as a fundamental element for ensuring the effectiveness of its compliance programmes and is committed to guarantee that all its activities are conducted in an ethical manner and with the utmost integrity. For this reason, the Company encourages its employees and anyone having working relationships with the organisation to report any suspected misconduct, with the guarantee of full confidentiality. ## JUVENTUS ACADEMY AND ITS CONTRIBUTION TO SOCIAL AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT

In the context of the positive impacts generated by its activities and with particular regard to the "Development of initiatives aimed at contributing to the social and cultural development of the territory", Juventus recognises the importance of its role in the social and cultural growth of communities, both locally and internationally. With this in mind, the Juventus Academy project is a strategic tool for the dissemination of sports values, the promotion of inclusion and the educational development of young people.

## THE JUVENTUS ACADEMY PROGRAM IS ACTIVE IN OVER 60 COUNTRIES

and aims to convey, through football, values such as respect, fair play, collaboration and sacrifice, contributing to the full development of children aged 5 to 17, regardless of their starting level. This educational approach aims to combine technical and athletic improvement with personal growth, with a focus on the players' mental and physical well-being and the building of a sense of belonging and active citizenship.

Through a widespread network of Academy and International Camps, Summer Camps, Training Experiences, residential programs and an international tournament,

![img-122.jpeg](img-122.jpeg)

JUVENTUS ACADEMY ALLOWS THE CLUB'S METHOD AND VALUES TO REACH CONTEXTS THAT ARE ALSO GEOGRAPHICALLY DISTANT, BUT UNITED BY THE DESIRE TO CREATE A POSITIVE IMPACT IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES:

AN OPPORTUNITY TO STRENGTHEN THE CONNECTION WITH THE TERRITORY. PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF YOUNG PEOPLE AND BUILD A LASTING VALUE HERITAGE.

This initiative is aligned with the Black, White & More strategy and, in particular, with the "Sustainable Glocal Club" pillar, which promotes the link between global vision and local action, integrating football into educational and social projects consistent with the Club's identity.

### THE PROJECT

The history of Juventus speaks for itself: a history stretching over 100-years of triumphs that have made the Juventus strip legendary and an audience of millions of fans around the world. It is no coincidence that "Juventus" means "Youth": founded by young people, always pursued by young people, Juventus combines historical heritage with objectives that are always at the forefront of a teaching method that aims to convey values that go beyond the pitch.

The Juventus Academy project was founded to take Juventus colours, method and values all over the world and to as many boys and girls as possible; it offers both the teaching and development of football skills and educational training, accompanying young players

220 | Annual Report as at 30 June 2025

221 | Juventus Football Club S.p.A.

--- pág. 112 ---

JUVENTUS

in their growth, from the introduction to the game to maturity, not exclusively in sports terms. All programs are available irrespective of participants' level and activities are based on respect for their mental and physical well-being. Fun is at the heart of all proposed activities. Starting from the recreational and creative aspect of football play, players are involved in activities intended to foster their all-round development in a safe and secure environment. Activities are based on respect for the physical and mental well-being of young people, to help them become independent. The principles underlying the project are:

- To have fun, entertain fun and share.
- To promote self-confidence and fair play.
- To learn to win and lose with equal dignity.

# JUVENTUS WAY

Following its philosophy, Juventus aims to train players through a vision that combines technical aspects and mental, emotional and relational aspects. This methodology can be summarised into five points:

- Play style: The desire to command and conduct the match: the pleasure of maintaining ball possession, the ability to peacefully manage the game and its timings, and the development of a team mindset based on resourcefulness and common sacrifice are fundamental.
- Technical abilities: Through special technical moving exercises, the Club aims to perfect football technical movements: from transmission to control, from space search to fast ball play in ball command.
- Tactical abilities: When talking about tactical capabilities, both individual and team skills are taken into account. These skills are trained with exercises that, alternately during the week, explore the principles of play. And principles of play mean the building, management and maintenance of control, refining and finalisation, and the defensive phase. The methodology uses simple and complex situational training methods, position games, control exercises and training matches.
- Mental aspect: The aim is the training of a player who is ready to make effective decisions, even in difficult and changing situations. In other words, the development of "Quick Thinking", the basis for best adapting to all situations and mutations that a match presents.
- Emotional-relational aspect: Sacrifice, courage, collaboration: these are the values that player must share, developing the concept of belonging and

team spirit. These are the values that underpin not only the work of players, but also of those who constantly follow them and accompany them in their growth, on and off the pitch.

# THE OBJECTIVE

Therefore, the future is represented by young people: this is why the Juventus Academy project is crucial. The philosophy underlying the proposal for children is based on combining the growth of the individual as a person to the methodological and more strictly "pitch" aspects. The objective is to help children to become the best they can be, confident that sport and football in particular are fundamental to convey educational values.

# Respect, spirit, education

At the heart of the project are respect for teamwork, the spirit of sacrifice, and education: an educated child, encouraged to act responsibly, will be a future adult ready to enter the world of work and act within society the best they can. Always, of course, with a view to respecting others. In short: growing people before players. The Juventus Academy project is open to young people aged 5 to 17 years, regardless of their level of play, who want to wear the Juventus black and white strip, in a less demanding and selective context than that of the Youth Sector, but based on the same values.

# THE PROGRAMMES

# Summer Camp

Among the main training projects promoted by Juventus Academy, Juventus Summer Camps ("Summer Camp") represent an initiative with a strong educational and social impact, offering children aged 8 to 17 years the opportunity to participate in an immersive summer experience dedicated to football, fun and sports values.

Organised in various carefully selected Italian locations, the Summer Camps offer high-level technical activities conducted by certified Juventus staff, in a stimulating, safe and inclusive environment. The initiative is designed to promote not only football development, but also the personal and relational growth of participants, contributing to their mental and physical well-being.

The programme also envisages specific courses dedicated to:

- young goalkeepers, with sessions aimed at perfecting technical and cognitive skills related to this highly specialised role;

- young female players, thanks to weeks of exclusively female training at selected venues (Masterclass, Chianciano Terme, Pinzolo), with the aim of promoting the active participation of girls and promoting gender equity in the sport.

Juventus also offers Summer Camp experiences outside of the national borders, as in the case of the prestigious programme implemented in Bath (Somerset, England).

# Academy International

The International Academy programme represents the global extension of the Juventus Academy project and is active throughout the year in over 90 international venues, with the aim of promoting technical methods, educational values and the Club's identity well beyond Italian borders.

Designed for children of different ages and levels, the programme adapts technical and training content to the local context, maintaining high quality standards thanks to the presence of technicians trained in Turin and the ongoing support of the Juventus Academy staff, who regularly oversees and visits the Academies around the world.

Through a structured and ongoing training path, young players are accompanied in their football and personal development, with a particular focus on mental and physical well-being, the development of their identity and the growth of values. The programme is based on three main principles:

- Passion for the game and learning.

- Fun as a lever for engagement and motivation.

- Professionalism, understood as care and rigour in the methods applied.

The programme represents a bridge between cultures, capable of strengthening the sense of belonging to the Juventus global sport community and to contribute to social development in the territories involved, through sport as a universal education and active citizenship tool.

The International Academies are active in numerous countries and cities across all continents, including: Abu Dhabi, Amman, Saudi Arabia, Armenia, Athens, Bahrain, Bogotá, Brazil, Chile, Cyprus, Washington DC, Devon, Dubai, Ghana, Guatemala City, Hong Kong, Houston, Indonesia, Kuwait, London, Los Angeles, Malta, Melbourne, Miami, Morocco, Moscow, Nanjing, New York, Nigeria, Oman, Panama, Perth, Piekary Slaskie, Qatar, RAK, Sadat City, Shanghai, Sharjah, Sydney, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Tokyo, Toronto, Torun, Tsalenjikha, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, Vaud, Wales, and Warsaw.

With the International Academy, Juventus strengthens its educational vocation on a global scale, promoting access to qualified sports paths and contributing to the social and cultural growth of new generations all over the world, in line with the principles of the "Sustainable Glocal Club" pillar.

# Juventus Academy Residency

The Juventus Academy Residency programme represents excellence in the Juventus training programme, offering young players from all over the world the unique opportunity to live, study and train in Turin for an entire academic year or for a semester.

This initiative, which combines a sporting, educational and cultural dimension, allows participants to experience the life of a young Juventus player, coming into direct contact with the Juventus Academy official technical staff and benefiting from professional infrastructures, such as the JTCV, as well as certified school courses at the J-College and WINS.

The programme is organised to ensure the whole round education of the individual through:

- professional training sessions with Juventus Academy technicians;
- participation in friendly matches and tournaments;
- study of the Italian language;
- full-board accommodation in a historic campus;
- educational and cultural visits (Allianz Stadium, Juventus Museum);
