Young players from different cultural backgrounds live through an immersive experience that promotes intercultural exchange, autonomy, emotional and relational management, as well as integration into an international environment. The proposed path aims to accompany each participant along a personal and sporting growth path, providing useful tools for managing future challenges both on and off the pitch.

Consistent with the principles of the "Sustainable Global Club" pillar, the Academy Residency represents a concrete example of how Juventus invests in the training of young people and the enhancement of human capital, also through dialogue between cultures, the promotion of education and the building of bridges with international communities.

# Training Camp

Juventus Academy Training Camps offer participants the opportunity to experience an authentic Juventus experience in selected international locations, combining high-quality technical training with opportunities for fun and socialisation.

# Training Experience

The Juventus Training Experience is a highly customisable formula, aimed at sports and school groups that wish to immerse themselves in the Juventus world. Each experience is tailored in collaboration with the Academy team, including:

- technical and tactical training sessions conducted by certified coaches;
- friendly matches;
- visits to the Juventus Museum and Allianz Stadium;
- opportunities for cultural discovery in Turin and other Italian cities;
- full board accommodation in hotels in Turin.

The programme is mainly carried out at the Juventus Academy Training Center in Cantabaja, a structure immersed in nature and equipped with excellent sports facilities, identified to ensure technical quality, safety and inspiration.

# Resort Experience

Within the Juventus Academy panorama, the Resort Experience represents an exclusive format that combines the excellence of Juventus training with the uniqueness of the most renowned resort locations. Through the Juventus Training Sessions, children and young people have the opportunity to experience summer as real protagonists, combining sport, relaxation and fun in an educational and unforgettable experience.

The programme brings Juventus' official teaching methods into exceptional seaside and naturalistic locations, such as Chia Laguna in Sardinia, the prestigious Verdura Resort in Sicily and the iconic Hotel Cala di Volpe on the Costa Smeralda. Selected for their beauty and accommodation quality, these locations offer the ideal setting to experience sports and well-being opportunities in contact with nature and the sea.

Each session is led by highly skilled Juventus Academy technicians, who ensure a high level of training, in line with the Club standards. Field activities focus on the technical, physical and behavioural development of the participants, enhancing team game and learning through fun.

The Resort Experience thus represents an extraordinary opportunity to train with the Juventus methodology also during the summer holidays, strengthening the Club's educational values in a relaxed, safe and inclusive environment, and so contributing to making every stay a significant step in the personal and sporting growth of young players.

# S3-1 – POLICIES RELATED TO AFFECTED COMMUNITIES

As also stated in its Code of Ethics, Juventus seeks to build, maintain and develop a relationship of trust with its stakeholders and bases its business model on the highest ethical and moral principles, inspired by key national and international best practices and aligning itself with the values of the Global Compact promoted by the UN and the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises. The Company recognises the central role of sport in social integration, in the promotion of mutual respect and social equity, and is committed to being a benchmark for its community in the broadest sense. Below are the policies adopted to protect the affected communities.

# SAFEGUARDING POLICY

Juventus has developed a Safeguarding Policy, with the aim of ensuring the protection of its registered players and technical staff, particularly those underage. The Policy is also intended for anyone who comes into contact with the Juventus registered players and technical staff, especially if underage, in detail:

- company staff and other collaborators, including occasional ones;
- staff of the Juventus Academy located throughout Italy;

- Juventus partners staff, such as:
  - Brand Development projects (e.g. Summer Camp, International Academies, Training Experience, World Cup, etc.), in various geographical areas in the world;
  - Fan Entertainment projects (e.g. Bimbi in Campo, Junior Photographer, etc.);
  - ESG projects (e.g. Gooca con Me, Juventus One, etc.) with respect to which Juventus has a collaboration relationship with external organisation (e.g. associations, non-profit organisations, etc.).

For further information on the targets, scope and purposes, please refer to section G1-1 – 'Corporate culture and business conduct policies'.

# PROCEDURE FOR 'MANAGEMENT AND DISCLOSURE OF INSIDE AND MATERIAL INFORMATION'

Pursuant to Article 17 of the MAR, the Company communicates to the public, as soon as possible, the inside information that directly concern the Company, in a manner that allows rapid access and a complete, correct and timely evaluation by the public, in compliance with the principles of fairness, clarity and equal access to inside information. The Corporate & Finance Managing Director is responsible for the management of inside information.

# PROCEDURE FOR THE 'MANAGEMENT OF TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES'

In implementation of Article 2391-bis of the Italian Civil Code and of the Regulation adopted by Consob with resolution no. 17221 of 12 March 2010, as subsequently amended and supplemented (Consob RPT Regulations), also taking into account, inter alia, Consob communication no. DEM/10078683 of 24 September 2010 and the Corporate Governance Code, the Company has adopted the Procedure for 'Management of transactions with related parties'. This document defines the rules relating to the identification, investigation, approval and performance of transactions with related parties concluded by the Company directly or by way of subsidiaries, as defined in the Appendix to Consob RPT Regulation. The Corporate & Finance Managing Director is responsible for the management of this procedure.

### S3-3 - PROCESSES TO REMEDIATE NEGATIVE IMPACTS AND CHANNELS FOR AFFECTED COMMUNITIES TO RAISE CONCERNS

Juventus has also established dedicated channels to allow stakeholders in its own community to report needs or concerns directly. To this end, Juventus provides all stakeholders with a reporting channel, accessible online at the public webpage: https://juventus.segnalazioni.net/ dedicated and secure, through which it is possible to report breaches of company laws, regulations, procedures and policies or to report, more generally, situations of potential risk.

This system protects the identity of the whistleblowers and guarantees the confidentiality of reports, which are visible only to the Whistleblowing Committee, which handles them in accordance with the principles of impartiality and confidentiality. In addition, the Company has put in place strict measures to prevent any form of retaliation against those reporting through the channel. Juventus prohibits such acts, whether direct or indirect, against the whistleblower, and envisages disciplinary sanctions against anyone who violates this prohibition or the obligations to protect the confidentiality of the whistleblower's identity.

For further details, please refer to section G1-1 – "Corporate culture and business conduct policies (Whistleblowing Management)".

### S3-4 - TAKING ACTION ON MATERIAL IMPACTS ON AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, AND APPROACHES TO MANAGING MATERIAL RISKS AND PURSUING MATERIAL OPPORTUNITIES RELATED TO AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THOSE ACTIONS

Aware of its social role and its strong national and international links, Juventus promotes concrete interventions to meet the emerging and structural needs of the communities it engages with. The Club's commitment translates into continuous or timely initiatives, developed in collaboration with third sector players, institutions and partners, aimed at generating shared value and contributing to a fairer and more inclusive society. These actions are part of the "Black, White & More" ESG strategy (ref. "Sustainable Glocal Club" pillars) and address material risks and opportunities, with particular attention to minors, persons with disabilities, subjects in fragile conditions and vulnerable educational contexts.

# JUVENTUS ONE

Juventus One is Juventus' Paralympic project. Established in 2017 with the name "Juventus for Special" and developed in collaboration with the local partner ASD Nessuno Escluso, this is a project with a dual - sporting and social - intent designed to promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities through football. It represents a concrete and courageous response to a still too traditional view of disability and its relationship with the sport.

THE PROJECT IS BASED ON A PRINCIPLE AS SIMPLE AS IT IS ESSENTIAL: DISABILITY IS NOT A LIMITATION, BUT ONE OF THE MANY CHARACTERISTICS OF THE HUMAN CONDITION.

Based on this awareness, Juventus One aims to break down prejudices, stereotypes and sanctimonious attitudes often associated with disability, restoring the central role, dignity and opportunities of expression to disabled persons.

Understood in its widest meaning, inclusion is the real objective: to recognise equal rights and equal dignity for all people in daily life as well as in sport.

Football plays a central role in this process. The young people participating in the project experience an authentic competitive experience: from qualified coaching staff to weekly training sessions, from locker room management to the selection of players for each match. The players are athletes in their own right, and as in every team, one's place on the pitch is won through commitment, constancy and performance.

This approach has proven successful from both a sporting and a human point of view. The sense of belonging to Juventus One strengthens the self-esteem and awareness of the players who go onto the pitch with the desire to improve, build relationships, overcome their limits – and to do so proudly wearing an important strip, that of Juventus.

FROM 2017 TO DATE, THE PROGRAMME HAS GROWN SIGNIFICANTLY: FROM ABOUT 40 PLAYERS TO THE BEGINNING, THE 2024/2025 SEASON INVOLVED 125 PLAYERS WITH COGNITIVE, RELATIONAL AND SENSORY DISABILITIES, DIVIDED INTO 7 TEAMS, TAKING PART IN THE PARALYMPIC AND EXPERIMENTAL FOOTBALL DIVISION ("DCPS") CHAMPIONSHIPS.

# FOCUS | PARALYMPIC AND EXPERIMENTAL FOOTBALL DIVISION

The DCPS was created with the target of enabling persons with disabilities to enjoy football, recognising the sport's strong social utility. It organises seven-a-side football competitions at regional level, structured into several categories and with national finals. The DCPS divides teams into four levels (A, B, C and D) according to the participants' skill.

The top ranked regional team of each level advance to the national finals. The current Juventus One structure includes:

- 1 team at first level;
- 2 teams at second level;
- 2 teams at third level;
- 2 teams at fourth level.

# THE THREE DIMENSIONS OF THE JUVENTUS ONE PROJECT

The Juventus One project is expressed into three fundamental dimensions, which together define its identity and social impact:

# 1. Sporting/competitive dimension

The project core, this dimension includes participation in the official competitions of the FIGC DCPS.

In the 2024/2025 season, the first-level team won the Piedmont-Lombardia interregional tournament, qualifying for the national finals in Tirrenia, where it played

a very exciting final - of high technical level - against the team Insuperabili.

The value of the group was confirmed by their victory at the Tardini For Special (7-8 June 2025), the most important Paralympic tournament in Italy, organised by Parma Calcio and with 36 participating teams. In the same weekend, a second-level team triumphed in the Tuttingioco international tournament in Mantua. During the season, Juventus One teams also took part in a fourth level tournament in Ghent (Belgium), as well as in numerous other third and fourth level regional tournaments.

# 2. Educational dimension – Juventus One@School

Launched in the 2018/2019 season, the Juventus One@School programme involves players and staff in educational activities in schools, with the aim of conveying the message that disability is not a limitation, but one of the many facets of the human experience.

Laboratory activities, free of charge and suitable for all school bands (primary school, first and second level secondary school), offer direct and training experiences on the topic of disability.

IN THE 2024/2025 SEASON, THE PROGRAMME REACHED AROUND 520 STUDENTS IN 7 SCHOOLS, EXTENDING FOR THE FIRST TIME ALSO OUTSIDE PIEDMONT, WITH MEETINGS IN THE PROVINCES OF MILAN AND COMO.

The programme is described in more detail in the section dedicated to education and awareness-raising projects.

# 3. Recreational and social dimension (age 6-16)

Aimed at children and adolescents on the autism spectrum or with cognitive disabilities, this path aims to offer a safe, stimulating and inclusive space to develop often unexplored skills.

Active throughout the season and with around 25 participants, the project planned - for the first time - to be divided into two groups, according to age: "little ones" and "youths", to better meet individual needs.

The season ended with a final party, which was also attended by other groups active in Piedmont and Lombardy, promoting socialisation opportunities for girls and boys who often experience exclusion.

The testimonies received from parents are significant, such as the one from a mother who says:

"My son hated football because nobody ever let him play football in the park. He would then pull back and chose to stay home alone. Now, with this activity, he has learned the basics of football. Other children now come to call him to play. Now, when we go out, he is happy. He likes to go to the park to play with other children."

# JUVENTUS ONE: A NEW NAME FOR A RENEWED VISION

Understanding that disability is not a limitation or a "special" condition, but one of the many facets of human diversity, in the 2023/2024 season Juventus embarked on a journey to redefine the identity of its Paralympic project.

Thus Juventus One came to be, the new official name adopted since the 2024/2025 season, which marks a change in the paradigm: not a project for "special people", but an initiative that places everyone - without distinction - on the same level of dignity, value and belonging. "One" expresses the deep unity that binds all of the Club's souls in a single sports and human community.

A fundamental step of this path took place on 3 December 2023, on the occasion of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, with the symbolic event "Juventus IS JUVENTUS", organised together with the partner ASD Nessuno Escluso. During the initiative, the players of the Paralympic team played a friendly mixed level match with the female Under-19 players and the men's Under-19 and Next Gen players.

Through play, the event wanted to communicate a strong and universal message: just as

"Juventus" AND "JUVENTUS" ARE THE SAME WORD WRITTEN IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, ALL CLUB PLAYERS ARE PART OF THE SAME FAMILY, REGARDLESS OF GENDER, AGE OR CATEGORY - MALE, FEMALE, U18, U23 OR PARALYMPIC. JUVENTUS IS ONE, JUVENTUS IS ONE, JUVENTUS IS ONE.

The day ended with an opportunity for deep reflection, thanks to the "Disability Experience" reserved for Club employees. Through football tests designed to simulate certain sensory, physical or cognitive disabilities, participants were able to put themselves in the players' shoes and experience first-hand the challenge - and the value - of inclusion.

In the wake of the 2023/2024 event "Juventus IS JUVENTUS", a symbolic meeting and sharing opportunity was also organised in the 2024/2025 season: on 6 May 2025, Juventus One's top-level team played a friendly game in Cantalupa against Juventus Residency Academy team.

A valuable training opportunity for both teams, which ended with a shared dinner, strengthening the link between young players and promoting mutual understanding.

# SUPPORTING SAVE THE CHILDREN

**JUVENTUS CONTINUES ITS STRATEGIC COLLABORATION WITH SAVE THE CHILDREN, LAUNCHED IN 2018, WITH THE AIM OF SUPPORTING THE WELFARE OF YOUNG GENERATIONS AND COMBATING EDUCATIONAL INEQUALITIES.**

The partnership is based on a common commitment to ensure quality educational opportunities for children and adolescents in economically and socially fragile conditions. This objective is pursued through a series of projects and activities that focus on the growth and social inclusion of young people.

![img-132.jpeg](img-132.jpeg)

# FOCUS | SAVE THE CHILDREN

Save the Children is the most important independent international organisation that for over 100 years has been fighting to save children at risk and guarantee their future. Its mission is to ensure that every child can live, learn and grow in safety. In 2024 alone, Save the Children reached and supported more than 41 million children: they supported 166 projects in 75 countries, contributing to financing 145 humanitarian responses with a dedicated global fund. In Italy, thanks to the support of 86 partners and the implementation of 118 projects, they reached 179 thousand people, of which more than 137 thousand children and adolescents

among the most vulnerable, in the North and South of the country. The main areas of intervention are: education, health and nutrition, protection, combating poverty and food security, rights and participation. Across all thematic areas, the organisation carries out an important advocacy action to create consensus with the relevant stakeholders in order to achieve positive and lasting changes for children in Italy and in the world.

In the 2024/2025 season, the collaboration with Save the Children provided a comprehensive and significant activation plan. The plan envisaged:

FOCUS | EDUCATIONAL HUB ACTIVITIES

The activities of the education hub are summarised below, with a focus on results and figures for the 2024/2025 season.

ACTIVITIES OF THE 0-6 TARGET EDUCATIONAL HUB

During this period, the Educational Hub offered a wide range of services aimed mainly at women and children in vulnerable conditions. The activities include:

- L2 Italian language courses for women and mothers, organised at times and spaces compatible with family needs and with the possibility of participating together with their children;
- Creative and manual workshops for the creation of small items (soap bars, creams, textile accessories);
- Cooking and health workshops with the support of a nutritionist and providing a shared lunch;
- Artistic and cultural activities, including African dance, music and traditional singing;

- Guided tours to museums and city parks to foster socialisation and knowledge of the territory;
- Swimming pool and water parks days to promote well-being and water skills in children;
- Social-health prevention paths with female teams (gynaecologist, nurse, cultural mediator), with individual and group meetings on female health;
- Laboratory for early cognitive development aimed at children aged 3-5 years and their mothers, with recreational and educational activities to stimulate logical and mathematical intelligence;
- Reading out loud workshops to bring children closer to books and raise parents' awareness on the importance of reading in the family;
- Emotional path guided by a psychologist, using art, music, stories and photographs to foster emotional expression;
- Baby massage courses for parents with children from 1 to 11 months;
- Orientation sessions to facilitate access to educational and social-health services and online resources;
- Theme-based meetings with paediatricians, nutritionists, educational consultants and experts on topics relevant to families.

In 2024, the number of new people welcomed during the year was 866 adults and 425 minors.

ACTIVITIES OF THE 6-17 TARGET EDUCATIONAL HUB

In 2024, more than 787 participants attended the activities of the Educational Hub. The Hub welcomes youths and minors from primary and secondary schools in the area for after-school support and to provide educational, artistic and social opportunities useful for personal growth and the development of soft skills. The main initiatives included:

- Study support: guided by adults/tutors and aimed at making young people autonomous and involved in their learning, it is carried out both in-person and through DAD (distance learning). It also includes sessions encouraging reading and workshops for the recovery of mathematical and linguistic skills, and is based on teaching methods that are inclusive

# EDUCATIONAL PROJECTS AND AWARENESS-RAISING ACTIVITIES: THE IMPACT OF FOOTBALL AS A LEVER FOR SOCIAL CHANGE

Football, with its unique ability to speak to millions of people of different cultures, ages and backgrounds, is an extraordinary vehicle for inclusion, awareness and social transformation. In an increasingly complex global context, sport can make a significant contribution to responding to collective challenges such as educational poverty, discrimination and marginalisation. However, this impact cannot ignore dialogue with local communities and collaboration with reliable third sector partners, which ensure its tangibility and continuity.

Juventus is fully aware of the responsibility that comes with its global visibility, witnessed by a digital community that exceeds 190 million followers worldwide. This wide scope implies the burden – and honour – of using its channels and institutional voice to promote positive values, actively and consistently contributing to the social development of the local areas with which it comes into contact.

# JUVENTUS ONE@SCHOOL

# JUVENTUS ONE@SCHOOL IS A FORMAT OF WORKSHOPS HELD BY THE ATHLETES AND STAFF OF JUVENTUS ONE TERMS IN LOCAL SCHOOLS, OFFERING STUDENTS A DIRECT, EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE ON DISABILITY.

The activity is carried out in-person and is designed for students in schools of all levels (elementary, middle, high school) in two phases:

a. The first phase is experiential and takes place through the reproduction of different types of disabilities in the gym. This activity aims to give girls and boys a direct experience of the sensations that an athlete with a disability feels when playing football;
b. The second phase, on the other hand, involves comparison through a series of testimonials and stories. The goal is to share and normalise their experience by breaking down disability-related prejudices.

Each meeting concludes with a collection of reflections on the experience. Often a clear awareness emerges of their own stigmatising outlook and how preconceived notions hinder the inclusion of friends, peers and persons with disabilities.

of which:

- 10 primary school classes;

- 5 senior high school classes.

Two classes of about 50 students from the University were also reached, for a total of 520 students.

GIOCA CON ME

"GIOCA CON ME" IS ONE OF JUVENTUS' SOCIAL PROJECTS TO PROMOTE SOCIAL INCLUSION THROUGH FOOTBALL, OFFERING CHILDREN FROM FRAGILE SOCIO-ECONOMIC BACKGROUNDS A SOLID OPPORTUNITY FOR PARTICIPATION, PERSONAL GROWTH AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF INTERPERSONAL SKILLS.

Active since 2012/2013, the project is based on an educational approach that integrates non-competitive sporting activities with social learning moments, aimed at fostering respect, collaboration and solidarity.

In the 2024/2025 season, Juventus renewed the project in collaboration with the Villa Sole Cooperative, involving 12 children between 7 and 9 years old, of which 9 males and 3 females, indicated by the Social Services of four districts of the city of Turin.

Workouts took place at the renovated ASD Campo Luini, located in the Lucento/Vallette area, equipped with latest generation synthetic grass fields, equip-

ped changing rooms and evening lighting. The choice of the venue has improved the quality of the sporting environment, while ensuring territorial proximity to the participants' areas of residence.

The programme is structured in 26 weekly sessions, coordinated by a dedicated staff consisting of:

- 1 project coordinator;
- 1 professional educator;
- 1 "Gioca con Me" instructor.

The educational method incorporates elements of psychology, play and sport, to encourage the development of physical, emotional and relational well-being. As Gerardo Quintana, a project instructor, reveals: "Psychology, football and education meet and come to life in the beauty of being together. Within this framework, we deploy playful exercises that stimulate learning and well-being in all its forms."

The project beneficiaries also had the opportunity to participate in non-sporting experiences designed to strengthen inclusion and a sense of belonging:

- access to the event "Bimbi in Campo & Junior Photographer" at the Allianz Stadium;
- participation in the Kings World Cup Nations Finals;
- visit to an open training session of the First Team.

In total, activities outside the field involved more than 30 children, with the word "happiness" as the most recurrent emotion in their stories.

In May 2025, Juventus also donated a wide supply of clothing for girls, boys, youths, guests and volunteers from the Villa Sole Cooperative, thus also contributing to meeting effective material needs.

# PHILADELPHIA JUNIOR CUP – “KEEP RACISM OUT”

On 26 March 2025, Juventus hosted the Turin leg of the “Philadelphia Junior Cup”, a national Under-14 seven-a-side football tournament promoted by Lega Serie A, dedicated to youth teams from cities with top-flight clubs and focused on the message “Keep Racism Out”.

The initiative involved young players from the Immacolata Concezione and San Donato parishes, engaged in a sporting but also educational experience, enriched by a moment of dialogue with two exceptional Club representatives:

- Michele Di Gregorio, goalkeeper of the Men’s First Team;
- Cecilia Salvai, defender of the Women’s First Team.

During the meeting, reflection took place on the importance of respect, friendship, teamwork and the fight against all forms of racism and discrimination, in line with the values at the heart of the tournament and the Juventus ESG strategy.

Following this, the Club invited participants to a special “Walk About” activity, organised prior to the Juventus-Genoa match (29 March 2025): a guided tour to discover the symbolic places of the Allianz Stadium and the most iconic moments in the history of Juventus.

38 girls, boys (12–14 years) and members of the educational staff took part in the initiative.

# CHANGE THE GAME

The first Italian association dedicated to preventing violence and abuse in sport, Change the Game, launched a training programme with Juventus in January 2025, aimed at coaches and staff working with male and female youth teams. The meetings on 20 February and 8 May 2025 provided operational tools to prevent and recognise situations of abuse, discrimination or unsuitable behaviour, contributing to the construction of a safe and respectful sporting environment. The initiative represents tangible action in line with the social responsibility of the Club and the protection of minors within its activities.

Fondazione Libellula

THE FONDAZIONE LIBELLULA IS A LEADING ORGANISATION IN ITALY FOR THE PREVENTION AND COMBATING OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND GENDER DISCRIMINATION IN ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXTS, WITH WHICH JUVENTUS HAS A WELL-ESTABLISHED RELATIONSHIP THAT BEGAN WITH THE AWARENESS-RAISING CAMPAIGN "BLOW THE WHISTLE ON VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN" IN THE 2022/2023 SEASON.

The Club was awarded the "Libellula Inspiring Company" recognition by the Foundation for this initiative. On 8 March 2024, the two organisations collaborated on the "More Women in Football" campaign, via which Juventus produced <b>tote bags</b> (thanks to the support of INDIVISA), with the proceeds going to the Foundation. Since the 2024/2025 season, Juventus has officially become a part of the <b>Libellula network</b>.

# INTERNATIONAL PROJECTS

Ghana: Girls Empowerment through Soccer

As part of its social impact initiatives, in Ghana Juventus supports the **Girls Empowerment through Soccer ("GETS")** project, developed by DGI Midtjylland - a non-profit Danish organisation - in collaboration with the local partner *Youth Opportunity and Partnership Programme ("YOPP")*. Active in rural communities in the north of the country, YOPP uses sport as a lever to develop and promote rights, especially in favour of women's empowerment.

GETS aims to **contrast phenomena such as early marriage, dropping out of school and teenage pregnancy** through the creation of a girls' football league and the activation of informal educational courses on sexual health, personal hygiene, family planning and gender equality. The training modules are held regularly in conjunction with the matches, directly involving the young participants.

In the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 seasons, the project saw the participation of **14 teams, divided into two groups, with more than 40 matches played between November and May**. To ensure quality and sustainability for the programme, the organisation has trained referees and coordinators, provided equipment and built an artificial playing field in one of the host villages.

On a parallel, the YOPP Girls League has promoted a series of actions to strengthen the impact of the project: participation in local radio broadcasts to raise community awareness, meetings with team representatives to define shared rules and values, and an important distribution of sports materials.

As emphasised by YOPP: "The integration of educational modules on sexual and reproductive health and related rights in the activities of the women's football leagues represents a valuable and effective strategy for reaching out to and empowering girls and women".

ITALY AND INTERNATIONAL SPECIAL OLYMPICS – WINTER WORLD GAMES IN TURIN 2025

ON THE OCCASION OF THE SPECIAL OLYMPICS TURIN 2025 WINTER WORLD GAMES, JUVENTUS CONFIRMED ITS COMMITMENT TO SPORTING INCLUSION BY WELCOMING A DELEGATION OF 137 SPECIAL OLYMPICS ATHLETES TO THE ALLIANZ STADIUM ON MONDAY 3 MARCH 2025 AND HOSTING A SYMBOLIC LEG OF THE TORCH RUN, THE TRADITIONAL RELAY RACE THAT PRECEDES THE START OF THE GAMES AND PASSES THROUGH SEVERAL ITALIAN CITIES TO BRING A MESSAGE OF UNITY AND HOPE.

![img-137.jpeg](img-137.jpeg)

The day was conceived as a genuine party of sports, values and sharing, culminating in the Juventus–Verona pre-match, where fans were able to meet Moly, the official mascot of the Games, participate in interactive quizzes and discover the mission of Special Olympics through moments of play and dissemination. A group of athletes and relay runners also took part in an exclusive guided tour of the stadium, with access to the Club's symbolic places.

The most exciting moment of the evening was held during the race interval, with the ceremony to light the torch on the pitch and the emotional testimonies of the athletes including that of Andrea Spezzano, triathlon champion, who declared: "It is a great honour to represent the Special Olympics athletes at such an important time for our country. The Torino 2025 Winter World Games are about sport, but above all else about culture: they wish to showcase our abilities and demonstrate what we are capable of, both in sport and in life. The torch that illuminates our way carries with it the flame of hope: the hope of a better future, in which stereotypes and prejudices are swept away."

This initiative represented a significant opportunity to activate the community and raise public awareness about the value of diversity and equal opportunities in sport, contributing to the creation of a more inclusive culture, in line with the Club's ESG values.

The action plan for the coming seasons should not be seen as a new set of activities, but rather as an improvement and refinement of existing measures, with the aim of gradually strengthening their effectiveness. At this regard, several of the programme targets reported in S3-5 – “Targets related to managing material negative impacts, advancing positive impacts, and managing material risks and opportunities”, which represent the basis of the development course that Juventus intends to undertake in the next few years, were defined.

# S3-5 – TARGETS RELATED TO MANAGING MATERIAL NEGATIVE IMPACTS, ADVANCING POSITIVE IMPACTS, AND MANAGING MATERIAL RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES

As part of its ESG strategy Black, White & More, Juventus has set specific objectives to strengthen the Club’s positive social impact on local and global communities, while reducing the risks associated with exclusion and inequality. These objectives are in line with

the “Sustainable Glocal Club” cornerstone and focus mainly on six areas of action:

# OBJECTIVE 1 | JUVENTUS ONE

Juventus One is the Club’s Paralympic project designed to promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities through football. Inclusion, understood in its truest sense, is the main objective: recognise equal rights and equal dignity for all people, in everyday life as well as in sport. With Juventus One, the Club aims to overcome prejudices, stereotypes and pitying attitudes that are still widespread, restoring centrality, dignity and opportunities for expression to the people who are part of it.

In this perspective, for the 2025/2026 season the Club’s target is to consolidate the figures achieved, with an increase of 10% compared to the average of the last two seasons, consolidating the quality and continuity of the project.

# OBJECTIVE 5 | ESG MODULE FOR JUVENTUS ACADEMIES

During the 2024/2025 season, Juventus initiated structured dialogue between the ESG Team and the Academy Team with the aim of integrating sustainability-related training content into the educational activities of the Academy programmes. The joint effort led to a shared assessment of an educational concept aimed at raising awareness among young participants

to on environmental and social issues, in line with the values promoted by the Club both on and off the pitch.

During the year, a number of small-scale pilot tests were launched - particularly in the Summer Camps - to experiment with effective methods and languages in the age group involved. The aim is to achieve, starting with the next summer edition, a genuine integration of educational modules on sustainability, contributing to the training of informed and responsible young citizens.

### S4-1 – POLICIES RELATED TO CONSUMERS AND END-USERS

Fans who use Juventus services at the Allianz Stadium (and at the Pozzo La Marmora Stadium in Biella for Juventus First Women’s Team matches; the Moccagatta Stadium in Alessandria for Juventus Next Gen matches) are required to observe:

- Regulations for using the facility: these are the rules of conduct and responsibility for fans, with the aim of ensuring safety, legality and inclusion. They regulate the use of admission tickets, the occupation of assigned seats, security checks and access for fans with disabilities. They establish restrictions to protect safety (discrimination, violence, dangerous substances and materials) and envisage sanctions in the event of violations. The document is approved by the Police Headquarters and the Juventus Event Management Delegate ensures its compliance and application.
- Code governing the transfer of admission tickets to football matches (Code of Conduct): the Code of Conduct regulates the transfer and use of tickets to football matches, ensuring that the stadium is a safe, welcoming place that respects the principles of legality, fairness and inclusion. Juventus rejects all forms of violence and discrimination, providing for injunctions (“satisfaction”) against those who adopt conduct contrary to these values. The measures protect fans, society and institutions, ensuring transparency, responsibility and respect for the rights of all spectators. The Company has set up a Committee made up of the Support Liaison Officer (“SLO”) and the Legal, Stadium & Consumer Business, Facilities Management and Communication Departments, which analyse behaviour and assess any sanctions.
- Form for requesting the display of banners, flags, use of drums or megaphones at the Allianz Stadium: this ensures transparency, safety and compliance with public safety and fire regulations. Fans must fill out an official form, attaching proof of identity and a graphic image of the banner, which is then evaluated by Juventus, in the person of the SLO and by the competent authorities for the issuance of authorisation; final approval is given by the Security Operations Group managed by the Police Headquarters. The authorisation ensures that the choreography complies with the rules of the Regulations for using the facility and does not contain discriminatory or dangerous content, thus protecting the safety, public order and rights of all spectators.

- General conditions for subscription of season ticket and sale of a temporary parking space for individual matches within the Juventus parking areas: these govern the purchase and use of parking spaces in the Juventus parking areas, as an accessory service to the stadium admission ticket. The rules guarantee contractual transparency, correct use of spaces and fan safety, defining purchasing procedures, access formalities, restrictions and user responsibilities. The regulations also establish clear limits (e.g., compliance with signage, prohibition of hazardous materials or improper use of spaces), sanctions for violations, and envisage the protection of personal data and the use of video surveillance in compliance with current legislation. The contact for this document is the Stadium & Consumer Business Department.

- People First Policy: the People First Policy, already described in the previous paragraphs, is referred to here as it also fully applies to fans, who are considered to all intents and purposes to be key stakeholders of the Club. In particular, this Policy – together with the previous ones – constitutes a tool for mitigating the risks indicated above (risk of violent or discriminatory behaviour by fans, with consequent reputational impacts and possible sanctions in accordance with sporting regulations; the risk to public order and security in relation to the methods of access and use of the Allianz Stadium during Match Days). Through the principles of inclusion, fairness and respect, as well as by means of effective prevention, awareness-raising and regulatory tools (which will be described below), the policy helps to ensure a safe and welcoming sporting experience for all. The People First Policy is also inspired by best practices and the main applicable regulations, guidelines and national and international documents on human rights, corporate social responsibility and corporate governance, including, by way of example, the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the main frameworks of the United Nations and the European Union.

Juventus has chosen to establish a direct and regulated relationship with its fan clubs through the recognition and management of Official Fan Clubs. Accordingly, the Club requires the signing of an annual service framework agreement, valid for each sporting season, which describes the services offered to all registered members and the general terms and conditions of membership.

Through a dedicated survey – the materiality analysis – Juventus was able to identify fans' perceptions, priorities and expectations regarding the environmental and social impacts generated by the Club's activities. The results obtained were a key factor in guiding the sustainability strategy, allowing for a more accurate definition of priority areas for action, consistent with shared values and with the evolution of the social and environmental context.

Furthermore, Juventus has actively involved its fans in measuring the Club's environmental footprint, particularly for the quantification of indirect greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 3). In fact, a survey was carried out to collect data that would help to estimate more accurately the impact of fan mobility during matches. The survey – carried out by Juventus' ESG Team – provided detailed information on various parameters, including: distance travelled to reach the stadium, frequency of attendance at sporting events, type of transport used and its fuel type (e.g. petrol, diesel, electric, hybrid, etc.). This data has been incorporated into the overall calculation of Scope 3 emissions, contributing to more comprehensive, transparent reporting based on actual evidence.

Through these initiatives, Juventus reinforces its desire to build constructive and ongoing dialogue with its fan base, making them an active part of the decision-making processes that guide the Club's sustainability process.

# JOFC DAY: AN OPPORTUNITY FOR ENGAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY

JOFC Day is one of the most significant tools Juventus uses to encourage the direct involvement of its fans and key stakeholders: the chairpersons and representatives of the approximately 530 Juventus Official Fan Clubs ("JOFCs") around the world.

The event, organised annually, has recently taken on an itinerant nature, moving away from its traditional Turin venue to take place directly in the areas where the clubs operate. This approach strengthens the sense of closeness and recognition vis-à-vis the local communities, making fans feel that it is Juventus itself that is "coming to their home".

The format includes two distinct moments:

- a recreational and social aspect, which encourages interaction between clubs and with the company, with dinners, entertainment and the presence of Juventus legends;
- an operational and discussion-related part, which addresses specific issues related to club management (activities, ticket sales, communication, services), but also opportunities for mutual feedback, in which Juventus takes on board the needs and proposals coming from the local areas.

IN THIS CONTEXT, FAN CLUBS ARE CONSIDERED TO BE GENUINE JUVENTUS AMBASSADORS IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THEIR MISSION GOES BEYOND SUPPORTING THEIR TEAM: MANY OF THEM PROMOTE SOCIAL, CULTURAL AND SOLIDARITY INITIATIVES, WORKING TOGETHER WITH CHARITIES AND ORGANISING ACTIVITIES THAT HAVE A POSITIVE IMPACT ON THE LOCAL AREA.

Through this tool, Juventus consolidates ongoing dialogue with its end-users, recognising them as key stakeholders in spreading the values of social responsibility, inclusion and participation.

# S4-3 – PROCESSES TO REMEDIATE NEGATIVE IMPACTS AND CHANNELS FOR CONSUMERS AND END-USERS TO RAISE CONCERNS

All feedback collected through the channels described above (including concerns, requests or grievances) is handled through a process that involves:

- receipt of the request;
- timely assessment of the feedback;
- involvement of the functions concerned for feedback management (e.g. Stadium & Consumer Business, ESG, SLO, DAO, Legal);
- implementation of solutions and improvements.

Juventus has also established dedicated channels to allow consumers and end-users to report needs or concerns directly. To this end, Juventus provides all stakeholders with a reporting channel, accessible online at the public webpage: https://juventus.seignalazioni.net/ dedicated and secure, through which it is possible to report breaches of company laws, regulations, procedures and policies or to report, more generally, situations of potential risk.

This system protects the identity of the whistleblowers and guarantees the confidentiality of reports, which are visible only to the Whistleblowing Committee, which handles them in accordance with the principles of impartiality and confidentiality. In addition, the Company has put in place strict measures to prevent any form of retaliation against those reporting through the channel. Juventus prohibits such acts, whether direct or indirect, against the whistleblower, and envisages disciplinary sanctions against anyone who violates this prohibition or the obligations to protect the confidentiality of the whistleblower's identity.

For further details, please refer to section G1-1 – "Corporate culture and business conduct policies (Whistleblowing Management)".

# S4-4 – TAKING ACTION ON MATERIAL IMPACTS ON CONSUMERS AND END-USERS, AND APPROACHES TO MANAGING MATERIAL RISKS AND PURSUING MATERIAL OPPORTUNITIES RELATED TO CONSUMERS AND END-USERS, AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THOSE ACTIONS

At the heart of Juventus' business lies the management and organisation of sporting events that bring together thousands of people simultaneously within the same facility. With one of the largest fan bases in the world, Juventus is committed to ensuring the safety of its sports facilities, in particular the Stadium and the adjacent commercial structures. Ensuring the health and safety of those who use the services offered by Juventus encompasses several aspects and must address multiple risks in order to maintain and strengthen the trust that guarantees the fulfilment of lasting and sustainable business objectives over time.

![img-145.jpeg](img-145.jpeg)

# THE ROLE OF THE SLO

In this context, a key role is played by the SLO - Supporter Liaison Officer, who is responsible for maintaining appropriate relations with the public. The purpose of this role is to build, maintain, consolidate and develop the club's "unique bond" with its supporters. This role, covered at Juventus by a dedicated resource, was introduced by UEFA to encourage clubs to improve their relationship with their supporters and to better organise their participation in events and initiatives. The main objective is to provide supporters and fans with a direct, two-way channel of communication with the Club.

This is a professional role introduced by UEFA in 2010 and adopted by the FIGC in its organisational criteria for obtaining national licences as a requirement for football clubs to participate in professional leagues.

The SLO acts as a point of reference for the public on various fronts: providing general information, receiving requests from fan groups, proposing initiatives and, more generally, being available to encourage the positive participation of supporters in the Club's activities. It is important to emphasise, based also on the latest provisions of the FIGC (see official statement No. 326/A and the reference to Article 12 of the code of sports justice – sub 9), that the SLO is the only official within the Club entrusted with knowledge of the supporters and "two-way" communication with them.

The SLO defines the Club's relationships with the fans and/or supporter groups; these relationships can become part of the Club's "life" thanks to the commitment of the SLO, who in turn liaises internally with all areas of activity. The definition of the SLO's role is the responsibility of each club's management, based on the specific characteristics of its organisation.

You can contact the SLO via the following e-mail address: slo@juventus.com

A fundamental step in this direction was the appointment of the DAO, a figure introduced in line with UEFA requirements. The DAO is responsible for coordinating and promoting all accessibility-related initiatives, hel-

ping to integrate the needs of fans with disabilities into the Club's policies and strategies. This role not only facilitates access and improves the experience of persons with disabilities within the Club's facilities and during sporting events, but is also part of a broader commitment to ensuring equal opportunities for participation and entertainment, strengthening the relationship with the fan base both physically and digitally.

Again with this in mind, Juventus has drawn up the "Terms and Conditions of the Accreditation Service for Fans with Disabilities", developed jointly by the Stadium & Consumer Business, People, Culture & ESG Departments and the DAO. This service provides free access to the men's First Team home matches for fans with 100% certified disability and, where applicable, their carers. The online procedure guarantees transparency and security through non-transferable, name-registered accreditations, with clear rules for application and access, as well as controls aimed at preventing abuse and ensuring the fair use of resources. In particular, the Allianz Stadium, home of Juventus, was designed to be an inclusive and accessible venue: it has 280 seats dedicated to persons with disabilities, allocated free of charge – by means of the procedure indicated above – to wheelchair users and fans with total disability who are able to walk, with the possibility of requesting free accreditation for a carer (to this end, the Club has reserved an equivalent number of seats). Accreditation is made on a first come, first served basis, given the limited availability.

To ensure safety and comfort, the dedicated sections (Tribuna Nord and Tribuna Sud) have been designed to meet the needs of wheelchair users and people with reduced mobility.

In addition to single match accreditations, it is also possible to purchase a discounted season ticket in the dedicated sectors, with prices announced each year as part of the Season Ticket Campaign.

During the 2024/2025 season, Juventus further enhanced its services, including through dialogue with the community of persons with disabilities, including the Ente Nazionale per la protezione e l'assistenza dei Sordi ETS APS ("ENS").

## SINCE AUGUST 2024, AN INNOVATIVE ITALIAN SIGN LANGUAGE ("LIS") TRANSLATION SERVICE HAS BEEN ACTIVATED FOR THE BENEFIT OF DEAF OR HEARING-IMPAIRED FANS.

The service covered the men's First Team pre-match press conferences (Serie A, UEFA Champions League, FIFA Club World Cup), as well as the national anthems and service messages broadcast at the Allianz Stadium during matches. Overall, 59 hours of LIS translation were provided during the season, coordinated by the DAO in collaboration with the Communication and Broadcasting & TV Production teams.

## FOR VISUALLY IMPAIRED SUPPORTERS, JUVENTUS HAS ALSO GUARANTEED AN AUDIO DESCRIPTION SERVICE FOR MATCHES DURING ALL HOME MATCHES PLAYED BY THE MEN'S FIRST TEAM.

This service is provided by a dedicated commentator positioned in the press box, who offers a detailed and accessible commentary of the sporting event.

The Club's commitment also extends beyond the stadium:

## THE JUVENTUS MUSEUM HAS BEEN DESIGNED TO BE FREE OF ARCHITECTURAL AND SENSORY BARRIERS

and offers tours dedicated to deaf, visually impaired or blind visitors. The experience is truly inclusive and immersive thanks to graphic and Braille panels, tactile supports, audio guides with descriptions and content in Italian Sign Language (LIS) that can be activated via embossed QR codes.

In conclusion, during open training sessions, Juventus reserves free places for fans with disabilities who have expressed a desire to participate, further strengthening its commitment to promoting the full participation of all fans in the sporting and social life of the Club.

By means of these measures, Juventus reaffirms its belief that inclusion does not mean creating separate spaces, but rather building a shared environment where everyone can feel like an integral part of the Juventus family. A commitment summarised by the message: "Juventus is ONE".

### INSTRUMENTS FOR IDENTIFYING DISCRIMINATORY BEHAVIOUR

On a parallel, in order to address the impact of "maintaining excellent standards for identifying discriminatory incidents within the stadium and on social media",

## AN INNOVATIVE SOFTWARE SYSTEM HAS BEEN IMPLEMENTED WITHIN THE STADIUM THAT ALLOWS FOR THE ACCURATE AND TIMELY IDENTIFICATION OF INDIVIDUALS RESPONSIBLE FOR DISCRIMINATORY BEHAVIOUR, ENABLING THE CLUB TO INTERVENE EFFECTIVELY.

Furthermore, Juventus has equipped itself with an automatic social media content monitoring tool that can detect and report comments containing hate speech, thereby helping to maintain a safe and respectful digital environment. In section S4-5 – "Targets related to managing material negative impacts, advancing positive impacts, and managing material risks and opportunities" the topic will be further explored, with a description of the specific measures and of the programme targets on the topic.

# COMMUNICATION CAMPAIGNS

In conclusion, the Club continues to encourage active and constant dialogue with its supporters, including through dedicated campaigns and engagement tools, with the aim of strengthening the sense of community and informed participation among fans. The action plan for the coming seasons should not be seen as a new set of activities, but rather as an improvement and refinement of existing measures, with the aim of gradually strengthening their effectiveness and alignment with international standards on human rights, safety and inclusion. At this regard, two of the programme targets reported in S4-5 – “Targets related to managing material negative impacts, advancing positive impacts, and managing material risks and opportunities”, which represent the basis of the development course that Juventus intends to undertake in the next few years, were defined.

# S4-5 – TARGETS RELATED TO MANAGING MATERIAL NEGATIVE IMPACTS, ADVANCING POSITIVE IMPACTS, AND MANAGING MATERIAL RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES

Juventus is against all forms of social and territorial discrimination, racism, xenophobia and violence, as stated in its Code of Ethics. Aware of its role as Football Company, this is why it confirms its commitment to the topic through solid actions.

The Club is constantly committed to ensuring its fans enjoy an inclusive, accessible and discrimination-free football experience, in line with the principles set out in the “People First” Policy and with the strategic cornerstone “Fan Centrality”. With this in mind, the Club has defined specific objectives and implemented tangible measures aimed at preventing negative impacts and reinforcing positive ones, contributing to the creation of a healthy and respectful environment both inside and outside the stadium.

The Club is committed to furthering an inclusive culture and environment, with the following objectives:

- ensuring a healthy environment that does not include any kind of expression of discrimination, including racial;
- guaranteeing equality and equity, valuing diversity;
- preventing and condemning harassment, gender-based violence and any other condition of discrimination, whether for issues of ethnicity, religion, personal belief, disability, age or sexual orientation.

Within the People First Policy, the “Zero Tolerance for Discrimination” approach is made explicit, finding effective implementation through specific measures:

# Zero Tolerance for Discrimination

Counter all forms of discrimination and racism, both on and off the pitch

Internal dimension (staff): Juventus does not tolerate any form of discrimination, exploitation, harassment, bullying, mobbing or isolation for personal or work-related reasons within its organisation. Such behaviour is punishable by disciplinary measures commensurate with the offence, with sanctions that may include termination of employment or collaboration. For further information, please refer to section S1-1 – “Policies related to own workforce”.

External dimension (fans | stadium): the Allianz Stadium has been equipped with a system of 86 Panomera multifocal videocameras that allow for the identification of individuals who engage in behaviour that is not in line with the Rules of use of the facility (and consequently with the Club’s values), which may result in a ban from Club events.

External dimension (fans | digital community): the desire to act on several fronts also involves the digital community. The Juventus ecosystem is one of the most popular digital ecosystems, and the Club’s aim is to build a healthy environment in which everyone can express themselves freely. For this reason,

The positive impacts and opportunities related to the topic G1 – Business Conduct are closely linked to Juventus' strategy and business model, which aim to promote a culture of ethics and integrity not only within the Company, but also throughout its value chain, contributing to the dissemination of responsible business practices with partners and stakeholders.

The commitment to ethical management strengthens not only company governance, but promotes constructive dialogue with stakeholders by improving the Club's reputation and consolidating the trust of fans, investors, institutions and local communities.

The effects of the risks associated with the business conduct topic concern criminal and administrative measures and sanctions and the deterioration of external perception. These risks could not only compromise the image of Juventus, but also negatively affect the trust of stakeholders by causing significant economic damage.

To prevent and mitigate these risks and strengthen its ability to generate value over the long term, Juventus has implemented a robust and transparent governance system based on policies and procedures that ensure compliance with regulations and the highest ethical standards

### G1-1 – CORPORATE CULTURE AND BUSINESS CONDUCT POLICIES

Juventus' corporate governance is geared towards protecting and maximising the Club's long-term value in pursuit of sustainable success, through the optimal management of resources in relation to strategic objectives, effective risk control, the highest level of transparency towards its community and the integrity of decision-making processes, in the interests of all stakeholders. Juventus acts with integrity, transparency, compliance with standards and zero tolerance towards any form of corruption to ensure the most correct management of the business and to establish relationships of trust and collaboration with all its stakeholders.

Juventus' model for responsible business conduct,

inspired by national and international best practices, is based on internal codes of conduct and a system of clear rules, periodically updated, which guide consistent and conscious behaviour, including the Code of Ethics, the 231 Model, the Prevention Model, the Safeguarding Policy and the Whistleblowing Management Procedure.

Also for the 2024/2025 season, Juventus reaffirms the centrality of Compliance as a key element of its organisational culture. The commitment is not limited to Health & Safety, but also extends to full compliance with regulations on corporate responsibility, to protect the integrity and sustainability of the work environment.

All mandatory training activities envisaged by current legislation have been duly provided, confirming a strategy oriented not only towards compliance with the law, but also towards the promotion of a safe, informed and responsible work environment.

During the season, particular attention was paid to training new company recruits, continuing the training programmes already started in previous seasons, with the aim of promoting awareness and understanding of the contents of the Organisational and Management Model pursuant to Italian Legislative Decree No. 231/2001 and the Prevention Model, thus reinforcing an approach in line with the Company's desire to consolidate a culture of risk awareness, in which training becomes a lever for prevention, accountability and continuous improvement.

Since January 2025, ad hoc sessions have also been provided in the company's induction plan.

Each session, tailored to the role and responsibilities of the resource involved, is designed to highlight the most relevant aspects in each case, so as to promote practical learning and raise awareness of the associated responsibilities and level of exposure to potential

# CODE OF ETHICS

The Code of Ethics represents the guidelines for ensuring the effective prevention and identification of any infringements of the law; it contains the general principles that cannot be departed from and is an integral part of the 231 Model and the Prevention Model, as well as a key element of the anti-corruption regulations. The latest update was approved by the Board of Directors on 23rd May 2024 and the updated version is available on the Company's website www.juventus.com.

Juventus undertakes to recognise and ensure compliance with the principles of conduct to be applied in the management of the Company's activities and, in compliance with this, all corporate bodies and employees of the Company, as well as all those who work towards the achievement of the Company's objectives are required to comply with these principles, each within the scope of their own functions and responsibilities. The Juventus Code of Ethics is inspired by best practices and the main applicable regulations, guidelines and national and international documents on human rights, corporate social responsibility and corporate governance, including, by way of example,

the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the main frameworks of the United Nations and the European Union.

The values established in the Juventus Code of Ethics commit all employees to ensure that the company's activities are carried out in compliance with the law, in a framework of fair competition, with honesty, integrity and fairness, respecting the legitimate interests of shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers, commercial and financial partners.

The Code of Ethics clearly and transparently defines the principles and values inspiring the entire company organisation:

- Impartiality and inclusiveness.
- Integrity.
- Integrity in the event of potential conflicts of interest.
- Transparency and completeness of information.
- Sustainability and social impact.

The Code also provides guidelines on issues such as corporate communication and confidentiality of information, personal data protection, insider trading, collections and payments, protection of company assets, crime prevention and internal organisational models, conduct in the performance of sporting activities and the implementation of the penalty system.

The issue of human rights is also of paramount importance when involving relations with external parties. Juventus avoids agreements with suppliers of dubious reputation that may not reflect the values expressed in this Code of Ethics in line with the principles of the Global Compact promoted by the UN, such as respect

# ORGANISATION, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL MODEL PURSUANT TO ITALIAN LEGISLATIVE DECREE 231/01

Following the entry into force of Italian Legislative Decree No. 231 of 8 June 2001, which introduced a system of administrative liability for companies into Italian law, Juventus' governance system was enhanced with the implementation of the 231 Model in accordance with the provisions of this legislation, which is updated on the basis of new regulations, such as the introduction or modification of predicate offences, or the operational and organisational needs of the Company. The last update of the Model currently in force was approved at the meeting of the Board of Directors on 23 May 2024, in acknowledgement, inter alia, of the regulatory changes, as well as for formal reference to the provisions of the FIGC Guidelines in the field of Safeguarding (C. U. 87/A FIGC of 31 August 2023).

As required by Italian Legislative Decree No. 231/2001, the role of the Supervisory Body ("SB") has been defined. This body is responsible for supervising and monitoring the functioning, effectiveness of and compliance with the 231 Model. This body is also the recipient of specific information flows, in accordance with the Model and the dedicated company procedure.

The 231 Model consists of a "General Section", individual "Special Sections" and some Annexes. In particular, the first part of the General Section opens with an overview of the relevant legislation and the related sanctions imposed on the Entity, followed by an introduction to the function of the Model and its operation within the Company. This is in addition to the SB functions, resource training activities and the dissemination of the model and the disciplinary system. The "Special Sections" of the 231 Model contain details on the categories of offences where

potential risk-offence profiles applicable to Juventus have been identified, following the identification of "sensitive" processes and activities.

The adoption and implementation of this Model is communicated to all the resources present in the company and a copy is available on the company Intranet portal, as well as on the Institutional Website for the "General Section" only. In addition, training activities are differentiated in terms of content and method of disbursement, depending on the qualification of the recipients and the level of risk in the area in which they operate.

# ORGANISATION, MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL MODEL PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 7.5 OF THE FIGC BY-LAWS

In addition to the policies described above, Juventus has implemented fundamental monitoring tools to identify, assess and address real or potential impacts related to its operations, integrating a culture of control and protection into its corporate and relational dynamics, including in the sporting arena, in order to effectively prevent and manage the risks associated with its activities and ensure conduct consistent with the Club's values.

In this regard, the Prevention Model is an integral part of Juventus' broader internal control and risk management system and, in particular, is coordinated with the 231 Model, following the guidelines of the Federation and the Lega Serie A Regulations. The adoption of the Prevention Model aims to improve the internal control and risk management system with specific reference to the prevention of unlawful sporting behaviour or behaviour contrary to the ethical principles of loyalty, fairness and integrity, as well as contrary to inclusiveness and fairness. The Prevention Model was adopted by the Juventus Board of Directors on 28 May 2020 and its updating is entrusted to the Guarantee Body. The last update of the Model currently in force was approved at the meeting of the Board of Directors on 25 June 2024, in acknowledgement, inter alia, of the regulatory changes, as well as for formal reference to the provisions of the FIGC Guidelines in the field of Safeguarding (C. U. 87/A FIGC of 31 August 2023).

## WHISTLEBLOWING MANAGEMENT

Juventus aims to promote a culture of fairness and legality and in this connection, in line with the provisions of Italian Legislative Decree No. 24/2023, has established its own whistleblowing channel and related Whistleblowing Management Procedure. Whistleblowing regulations, therefore, consist of a set of rules and procedures aimed at encouraging and protecting internal or external stakeholders who report illegal activities or irregularities of which they become aware, from retaliation and discrimination. The ultimate goal is to ensure that the Club receives an accurate flow of information that alerts it to situations of risk and to guarantee the timely management of whistleblowing reports, promoting an environment that helps to identify, prevent and combat the commission of offences and/or crimes, to protect the Company and its shareholders from economic damage, to safeguard their image and reputation, spreading a culture of ethics, legality and transparency within the Club, and strengthening the internal control and risk management system.

To this end, Juventus provides all stakeholders with a reporting channel, accessible online at the public webpage: https://juventus.segnalazioni.net/ dedicated and secure, through which it is possible to report breaches of company laws, regulations, procedures and policies or to report, more generally, situations of potential risk.

In particular, through the portal, it is possible to report:

- breaches of national and European Union regulations that damage the public interest or the integrity of the public administration or private entity, as referred to in the applicable regulations;
- violations of the Code of Ethics;
- violations of the 231 Model;
- violations of the Prevention Model;
- violations of the Safeguarding Policy;
- serious and/or repeated violations of internal procedures and regulations of Juventus, even if not explicitly referred to by the aforementioned Models or Code of Ethics;

- violations of laws and regulations (sporting and non-sporting) applicable to the sector in question;
- administrative, accounting, civil or criminal offences that do not fall under the previous points.

Reports received through the platform are viewed by those responsible for their management (independent external persons: the Chair of the Juventus' SB and the external member of the Juventus' Guarantee Body), authorised to process personal data pursuant to current privacy regulations, who will carry out an initial outline assessment of the violation information, in terms of:

- relevance of the situation described in relation to this procedure;
- the presence of sufficient information to carry out subsequent investigation activities.

Once the admissibility has been determined, the Managers will carry out a second preliminary assessment aimed at understanding the nature of the report in order to identify whether it concerns individuals inside or outside the organisation and, consequently, to assess which of the individuals indicated below should be involved.

The management and verification of the validity of the circumstances described in the Report, as well as the decision to

initiate any in-depth analysis or investigation activities, are entrusted to the Assessment Team made up of the Managers and any other associates involved in the management (e.g. Juventus employees, other external professionals) within the scope of their respective expertise, in order to ensure respect, impartiality and consensus.

Once all investigation activities have been completed and the assessment is carried out, corrective actions and/or any measures to be taken are defined. Finally, the report is closed and the related response is provided to the whistleblower.

This system protects the identity of the whistleblowers and guarantees the confidentiality of reports, which are visible only to the Whistleblowing Committee, which handles them in accordance with the principles of impartiality and confidentiality.

In fact, reports may be submitted by all the Company's stakeholders, including customers, suppliers, business partners, lenders, consultants, former employees and fans. In addition, the Company has put in place strict

![img-151.jpeg](img-151.jpeg)

measures to prevent any form of retaliation against those reporting through the channel. Juventus prohibits such acts, whether direct or indirect, against the whistleblower, and envisages disciplinary sanctions against anyone who violates this prohibition or the obligations to protect the confidentiality of the whistleblower's identity.

In the event that the Company finds cases of corruption, as also envisaged by the Whistleblowing Management Procedure, it must immediately inform the Control and Risk Committee, which in turn will inform the Board of Directors.

Furthermore, in order to monitor and manage the protection of personal data on an ongoing basis, several procedures have been adopted such as, for example, the Data Breach Management Procedure, the Privacy by Design By Default Procedure or the System Administrators Management Procedure. # G1-2 – MANAGEMENT OF RELATIONSHIPS WITH SUPPLIERS AND G1-6 – PAYMENT PRACTICES

Although suppliers do not represent a distinctive element of sports business as in other sectors, they play a key role in the value chain of Juventus (see ESRS 2 SBM-1 – Strategy, business model and value chain).

Juventus works every day to ensure that synergy between the Club and its suppliers develops and grows optimally, leading to genuine partnerships. For this reason, it intends to work together with suppliers that share the same values, focused on the development of and compliance with sustainability practices,

human rights and labour rights with a view to developing the overall well-being of society. In this regard, the tool used to verify supplier suitability is the Juventus Procurement Portal, which Juventus has developed and owns. In the qualification process, in order to be able to proceed with a purchase from a supplier, all Juventus suppliers must view and accept:

- the Code of Ethics;
- the Prevention Model;
- the Safeguarding Policy;
- the 231 Model;
- the Sustainable event management policy;
- the Juventus Environment Policy;
- the Medical sector quality policy;
- the Health and safety policy;
- the General terms and conditions for the purchase and/or supply of goods and/or services;
- the Terms and conditions for registration, access and use of the Juventus procurement portal;
- Disclosure on the processing of personal data.

It should be noted that external suppliers who provide specific services and activities on behalf of Juventus are identified as Data Supervisors pursuant to Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and operate in compliance with the instructions and contractual obligations set out in the "Personal Data Processing Agreement", drawn up in accordance with current legislation.

In its supplier evaluation process, Juventus now also considers environmental, social and governance sustainability criteria, such as, for example: the adoption of specific policies or regulations, the certifications held, and the publication of a Consolidated Sustainability Statement. Such criteria are currently mapped but have a non-priority impact.

In some cases, these criteria are more relevant, such as in the selection and confirmation of suppliers operating at the Club's various sites, where consideration is given to their ability to ensure correct waste management, including collection, sorting and disposal activities.

In addition, Juventus is migrating towards a new supplier management platform, with the aim of improving the overall efficiency of the system and introducing specific audits on partners' ESG profiles, thus strengthening the integration of sustainability criteria into

supply chain procurement and management processes.

During the 2024/2025 season, the Juventus supplier base comprises 1,476 business partners. The Club aims to maintain a balance between the use of local

skills and access to international best practices. In fact, in its supply chain management approach, Juventus has always given value to the local product and, as proof of this commitment, the figure for local suppliers is 81.03% of the total.

|  % suppliers Turin and province | 27.24%  |

The Company takes steps to pay all invoices past due and payable on a monthly basis, in line with contractual commitments undertaken. Payment terms vary according to agreements with individual suppliers, ranging on average between 0 and 60 days from the end of the month of the invoice date. It should be noted that, with regard to football clubs, in line with industry practice, the settlement terms extend beyond one year.

Any payment blocks may be activated in the following cases:

- non-presentation of mandatory tax documentation (e.g. DURC - single insurance contribution payment certificate);
- the presence of disputes open with the supplier.

It should be noted that, as of the date of preparation of this document, there are no pending legal proceedings vis-à-vis the Company relating to late payments.

Finally, for the purposes of the G1-6 – Payment practices indicator, the following is disclosed:

- the average time the undertaking takes to pay an invoice from the date when the contractual or statutory term of payment starts to be calculated, in number of days: 17,8 days¹⁶;
- the percentage of payments aligned with the standard Juventus terms (between 0 and 60 days): 40%.¹⁷

For this first reporting year, the analysis was focused on all transactions made by the Company, with the exception of those made by J Hotel (B&W Nest).

# G1-3 – PREVENTION AND DETECTION OF CORRUPTION AND BRIBERY

The zero-tolerance principle adopted by the Club is applied within the Models and policies described above. Juventus strongly condemns any behaviour that can be attributed to corruption, such as the abuse of a position to obtain an illegal advantage for the Club or the individual.

The Company prevents any problems in this respect mainly through: (i) careful risk analysis; (ii) the definition and implementation of policies and procedures; (iii) training and awareness activities for internal resources; (iv) structured internal control activities.

In particular, the Code of Ethics makes reference to the following regulations:

Juventus avoids agreements with suppliers of dubious reputation that may not reflect the values expressed in this Code of Ethics in line with the principles of the Global Compact promoted by the UN, such as respect for the environment, working conditions, human rights and the principles of legality, diversity and inclusion, respect for competition and the fight against corruption [...]

Juventus condemns any behaviour that may be construed as an act of corruption also with regard to private individuals, with regard to whom reference should be made to Article 7.6 below. Any attempt at extortion, official misconduct or inducement to give undue benefits by a public official or a civil servant must be reported without delay [...]

¹⁶ The indicator was calculated as the arithmetic average of the days of late payment associated with each payment made in the reporting period.
¹⁷ The indicator was calculated as the ratio of the number of transactions for which the standard payment terms (0-60 days) were respected and the total number of transactions.
